#1832. Where to watch Manchester United vs Roma: TV channel and live stream for Champions League today

The Standard's journalism is supported by our readers. If you click links to other sites on this page, we will earn commission.

Manchester United host Roma in the Champions League tonight as Michael Carrick desperately seeks an end to their woeful winless run.

The beleaguered Man Utd boss may now have only two games left to save his job, with a further review expected during the November international break, following Sunday’s home clash with Aston Villa in the Premier League.

Though his side delivered a much-improved first-half display against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge on Saturday, the wheels then swiftly fell off in familiarly chaotic fashion as Lisandro Martinez was dismissed in a 2-0 loss - United’s third in a row and fourth in the last five matches.

They have gone nine matches without a victory for the first time since the 1988/89 season to spark genuine concern over a potential relegation battle, having not won at all since their last Champions League home fixture - the 4-0 drubbing of Azerbaijani debutants Sabah FK on September 10.

But, having lost away at Atletico Madrid and Como since then to slip to 21st in the league phase table, they can expect a much sterner challenge from Roma, who continue to thrive despite a lengthy injury list that has seen them travel to Old Trafford with only 17 available outfield players.

The Giallorossi are in strong form under Gian Piero Gasperini and sit third in Serie A, still unbeaten and four points adrift of leaders Inter Milan after 10 games having won four of their last five matches across all competitions including Saturday’s 5-2 demolition of struggling Udinese.

Roma brushed aside Slovan Bratislava 4-0 in their last Champions League outing, having also been edged out by Real Madrid in a seven-goal thriller and drawn with Fenerbahce to sit 15th.

Carrick will hope to invoke the spirit of 2007, when he scored twice for United in a memorable 7-1 home trouncing of Roma in the Champions League quarter-finals.

TV channel and live stream: Unlike most Champions League fixtures, tonight’s game is not being shown live in the UK on TNT Sports.

Instead, it will be broadcast by Amazon Prime Video, who still have the first pick of one Tuesday night match up until the semi-finals.

Coverage begins at 6:30pm GMT ahead of an 8pm kick-off at Old Trafford, presented by Gabby Logan and featuring punditry from former Man United trio Wayne Rooney, Nicky Butt and Ashley Young.

#1831. Crystal Palace make decision over Jean-Philippe Mateta red card appeal before Liverpool

Crystal Palace have lodged an appeal against the red card awarded to Jean-Philippe Mateta during their 2-0 defeat to Tottenham last Saturday.

Mateta was sent off in the 13th minute, following a VAR review, for a studs-up challenge on Micky van de Ven as the pair contested for a loose ball at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

Referee Michael Oliver originally awarded Mateta a yellow card but upgraded his decision after being sent to the monitor to have a second look at the challenge.

With Palace down to 10 men, Spurs took control of the game and sealed a comfortable victory after goals in either half from Archie Gray and Jan Paul van Hecke.

Mateta landed on top of Van de Ven’s right ankle with his studs up as he chased a pass into space, and Oliver deemed the 29-year-old to have used “full forceful contact” as he explained his decision inside the stadium.

Palace’s view, though, is that Mateta’s challenge was accidental, and they argue that the French international had his eyes on the ball and did not see Van de Ven coming.

Mateta currently faces a three-match suspension, but Palace hope the decision is either overturned or his ban reduced.

Pierre Sage, who is under increasing pressure to turn things around at Palace, has only recently welcomed Mateta back into the fold after a hamstring injury and will desperately want his star striker back available.

If Mateta’s ban is upheld, he would miss this weekend’s home game against Liverpool, as well as crunch fixtures against newly promoted teams Coventry and Hull.

He will, however, be available for selection when Palace host Hoffenheim and Real Sociedad in the Europa League.

#1830. Liverpool confirm Ryan Gravenberch injury blow as Andoni Iraola names squad for Champions League clash

Liverpool have been dealt a new injury blow as Ryan Gravenberch will miss the Champions League showdown against Fenerbahce.

Gravenberch has cemented himself as a regular in Liverpool’s midfield since the autumn international break, starting five of the seven matches across all competitions.

He did, however, miss the comeback win over Brentford through suspension after being sent off in the defeat to Manchester City and was then dropped for the 1-0 loss to Arsenal at the weekend.

Gravenberch was expected to be in contention for Liverpool against Fenerbahce on Wednesday, but it has since been revealed that the Dutchman will not be making the trip to Turkey.

A Liverpool statement reads: “A heel injury means the midfielder will not be part of the Reds’ travelling squad for Wednesday’s meeting with the Turkish side in Istanbul.

“He will instead remain at the AXA Training Centre to undergo treatment with the club’s medical team.”

As such, Gravenberch joins Hugo Ekitike, Conor Bradley, Giovanni Leoni and fellow Dutchman Jeremie Frimpong as the five Liverpool injury absentees against Fenerbahce.

Iraola issued an update on the Dutchman on Tuesday: "It is a day to day thing.

“The fracture healed, it is about the pain. He has some discomfort. It is going to be something every day we will ask him how he is."

Wataru Endo and Federico Chiesa, meanwhile, are unavailable due to not being named in the club’s squad list for the Champions League this season.

It remains to be seen if Gravenberch will be fit to face Crystal Palace at the weekend, though he has a battle on his hands to regain a midfield spot from Trey Nyoni.

“The thinking is that he's playing very well and we trust him," Iraola told Sky Sports pre-match of his decision to drop Gravenberch in favour of Nyoni against Arsenal.

#1829. Joao Pedro double and Caicedo stunner give Chelsea win over AC Milan

Chelsea cruised to victory over Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan in Jakarta, Indonesia, on Saturday. Goals from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to their second win on their Far East tour.

The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Moises Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

The west London side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.

Just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

MOISÉS CAICEDO THAT IS INCREDIBLE 🤯 pic.twitter.com/C6CEcUG1sE

Chelsea had further chances to extend their lead in a dominant second-half performance but were unable to add to their three goals.

Chelsea conclude their tour of the Far East with a game against Johor Darul Ta’zim on Sunday in Malaysia before returning home.

Their final pre-season game will be against Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge before beginning their Premier League campaign at Fulham.

AC Milan take on Amorim’s former club Manchester United next Saturday before they kick off their Serie A campaign at Torino on August 23.

Chelsea managed to lure Austin MacPhee to take care of their set-pieces and today Chelsea scored two goals from corners. Here is a snippet of Mike McGrath’s piece on MacPhee’s arrival at Chelsea:

He is among the new breed of coaches who are rock stars in their own right, taking centre-stage since rules were changed so that only one person is allowed in the technical area at a time. For MacPhee to get closer to the players for a set-piece, it will mean Xabi Alonso taking a step back onto the bench.

It has been an incredible rise for MacPhee, 46, who was working on Michael O’Neill’s staff with Northern Ireland 10 years ago this summer, helping them reach the knockout stages of the European Championship.

Chelsea take on Johor Darul Ta’zim in Malaysia tomorrow before returning to the UK. Their final pre-season game will be against Real Sociedad before taking on Fulham on the opening weekend of the new season.

AC Milan will play Manchester United next weekend and then kick off their Serie A campaign against Torino.

The final whistle is blown in Jakarta and Chelsea have cruised to a 3-0 win over AC Milan. Goals from Caicedo and a double from Pedro either side of half-time have led Xabi Alonso’s side to the victory. They have one more game out in the Far East before returning home to the UK.

What a performance! 👏 pic.twitter.com/GcUZXwXbRj

Ramos is picked out after making a run into the Chelsea box and is denied by Sanchez. However, the offside flag has gone up anyway against Ramos. AC Milan have barely threatened the Chelsea goal in this second half.

Chelsea make a triple changes as Estevao, Mudryk and Watson come on. Mudryk made his return after his doping ban against Juventus during the week.

Jackson opens up his body as if he is going to curl his shot into the far corner but instead shoots towards the near corner, with his effort coming off the post.

Ricci goes for an audacious strike with the outside of his right foot from outside the box but his effort misses the target.

Palmer was deep in conversation with his boss Alonso during that water break.

Chelsea hit the post. Quenda receives the ball on the right side of the penalty area and quickly moves the ball onto his right foot. The 19-year-old then smashes a shot towards goal and the ball flies into the outside of the post. Quenda struck that with some venom.

Palmer has a chance to get Chelsea’s fourth from the left side of the box but AC Milan keeper Torriani makes the save down to his left.

AC Milan have offered very little going forward since the break and Sanchez has not been troubled in the Chelsea goal.

Palestra is found with a cross from the right to the far post. Palestra takes a touch but his shot goes into the side netting.

Ruben Amorim is demanding a free-kick just outside the Chelsea box but the referee does not agree. Replays show that AC Milan probably should have been given the free-kick as it was a foul by Fofana on Ramos. Both players went down but are back to their feet.

Caicedo hits it first time on the volley with the outside of his right foot and picks out the bottom right corner with perfection.

Chelsea go 2-0 up not even a minute into the second half. Neto, on the right side of the box, cuts onto his preferred left foot and crosses to the far post. Pedro gets on the end of it and, despite the Milan keeper getting a touch on the shot, the ball ends up in the far corner.

AC Milan have made a raft of changes at the break, which includes their new record signing Ramos, who has joined from PSG this summer. Former Chelsea man Nkunku is also on. Milan were back out from the dressing rooms a fair bit earlier than Chelsea were. It is rather farcical how long Chelsea took to re-emerge for the second half and they just saunter out as if nothing is up. Why on earth did the officials just allow Chelsea to take over 20 minutes for half-time?

Nearly 25 minutes after the first half concluded, we are finally back under way in Jakarta.

The first half in Jakarta is brought an end and Chelsea take a 1-0 lead into the break courtesy of Pedro’s goal on the stroke of half-time.

90 seconds into added time at the end of this first half, we have the first goal in Jakarta. Caicedo’s delivery from the right picks out Pedro, who has a free header inside the six-yard box and makes no mistake, picking out the corner. Pedro really should not have been afforded so much space in the six-yard box.

Palestra makes a run in behind the AC Milan defence and is found but De Winter gets back to put it behind for a corner...

Then, moments later, Pedro spurns a great chance for Chelsea. Palestra’s cross from the left is just out of Palmer’s reach but falls straight to Pedro, who blazes over from 12 yards out. He was leaning back and should really be hitting the target.

The space opens up for Palmer to take on a shot from range but his effort is blocked by De Winter. Palmer has not managed to have that much of an effect on this game thus far.

Neto takes a first-time shot from outside the box and looks to curl it into the far corner, forcing Torriani into a decent save diving down to his right.

That is good one-vs-one defending from Achemapong. Estupinan plays the ball into the path of Leao, who drives through the Chelsea half down AC Milan’s left. As Leao approaches the Chelsea box, Leao attempts to push it past Acheampong but the young Chelsea defender times his sliding challenge to perfection and puts it behind for a corner. Sanchez punches it out to the edge of the box, where Comotto takes it on his chest before volleying towards goal. The ball goes behind for another corner, which Chelsea just about scramble away.

Chelsea hit the post. Palestra drives forward for Chelsea down their left before the ball falls to Welbeck on the left side of the box. Welbeck’s effort hits the outside of the post. AC Milan keeper Torriani appeared though to always have it covered.

Chelsea gift the ball away inside their own half and Leao drives forward. The Portuguese forward moves into the Chelsea penalty area before getting his shot away but his effort is blocked.

A big, big chance for Chelsea to take the lead. A long ball is played forward in behind the AC Milan defence and Pedro gets the better of De Winter inside the Milan penalty area. It is then a one-on-one chance with Torriani but Pedro hits it straight at the Milan goalkeeper. Torriani should have come to claim that long ball and then Pedro should probably have buried that opportunity.

Chelsea win their third corner of the game as Palmer’s cross from the right takes a couple of deflections off AC Milan defender. Captain Caicedo has trotted over to take it out on the left. He sends it into a good area but a foul on the AC Milan keeper Torriani is given against Pedro.

Neto clips a free-kick into the AC Milan penalty area, which is chested down by Pedro. The Brazilian holds the ball up well inside the box before winning a corner. Chelsea play it short and Palmer crosses to the back post, where Palestra wins Chelsea another corner, this time out on the left.

Caicedo’s inswinging delivery is headed away at the front post.

Palestra, who has joined Chelsea this summer from Atalanta, is proving his versatility today; he has mostly operated for Chelsea at right-back so far this pre-season but he is starting at left-back in this game.

Camarda is played in behind the Chelsea defence and tries to get the better of Fofana inside the Chelsea penalty area but the ball just runs out of play across the byline before Camarda can square the ball.

We are under way in Jakarta, Indonesia, in Chelsea’s penultimate game over in the Far East. Before the game started, a huge AC Milan tifo was unveiled at one end of the ground.

It is 7pm in Jakarta yet the temperature is still up at 29 degrees with the humidity at nearly 70%. These conditions will be a proper test for both sides.

The teams emerge from the tunnel and we are just moments away from kick-off in Indonesia.

The trophies won by Franco Baresi, who has died at the age of 66, are their own monument to the AC Milan and Italy defender’s greatness. Six times a Serie A champion, five as captain, three European Cup-winning campaigns, 10 other winners’ medals and the distinction of being a member of Italy squads that finished in first, second and third places at World Cup tournaments demonstrate that his career, in a significantly more meritocratic era, stand alongside the giants even if the bias towards attacking virtuosos denied him the Ballon d’Or his talent deserved.

Yet they do not tell us why the grief, so tangible in Milan and beyond today, transcends tribal rivalry. It would be unfair to say that he transformed the art of Italian defending. Gaetano Scirea, the elegant Juventus sweeper who kept the 21-year-old Baresi confined to the bench when Italy won their third World Cup in 1982, had a surplus of natural ability, composure and intelligence. He did not need the raw-elbowed brutality of Claudio Gentile, heir to generations of Italian defenders influenced by the post-war influx of players brought up in the traditions of Argentina and Uruguay.

Chelsea’s pre-season continues out in the Far East as they take on AC Milan in the Gelora Bung Karno Stadium in Jakarta, Indonesia. Both clubs now have new managers, with Xabi Alonso taking over at Chelsea and former Manchester United boss Ruben Amorim now at the helm at AC Milan. These sides met in pre-season last year, with Chelsea winning 4-1 at Stamford Bridge. At that time, now-Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca was in charge whilst Max Allegri, who is now at Napoli, was leading AC Milan. The last time they met competitively was during the 2022/23 Champions League season, with Chelsea winning both games.

Chelsea lost 1-0 to AC Milan’s Serie A rivals Juventus on Wednesday in Hong Kong, in which Danny Welbeck made his first Chelsea appearance after joining from Brighton in the last week.

“We want to have a great team spirit and that is built on a daily basis with a great culture in the building,” Alonso said in his pre-match press conference. “That helps in the moment you have to compete. You feel better having that togetherness, trust, and the bonds between the players are so important to ultimately building a winning mentality, and a team that can compete anywhere. So the football side is so important, but the mental side is as important. And the strength of the team is the most important. We have been able to train and prepare [during pre-season] and I am very happy with the attitude and personality, we know that it is a very important part of this tour.”

It has been another busy week on the transfer front for Chelsea; not only has Welbeck arrived over the last week but so too have Jordan Henderson and Valentin Barco. Alonso’s men have two more games after this against Johor Darul Ta’zim and Real Sociedad before getting their Premier League campaign under way with a derby against Fulham at Craven Cottage.

AC Milan finished fifth in Serie A last season to earn a spot in the Europa League last season. Their big-money acquisition this summer as been Portuguese striker Goncalo Ramos from PSG. They have played two pre-season friendlies so far, which have both ended in draws; 2-2 against Celtic and then 1-1 against city rivals Inter. They kick off their Serie A campaign at Torino on August 23.

#1828. De Winter admits Milan ‘knew’ they could win with work still to be done: “To do things right”

Koni De Winter, before the start of the season, may not have expected to be central this season, but he’s been key to AC Milan.

With talk of another defensive arrival on the way, De Winter spent most of the summer seen as a back up. After all, Matteo Gabbia was there and there may have been another by the end of the window.

However, as we approach the halfway stage of the season, he’s been at the core of the Milan defence. Alongside Strahinja Pavlovic, he’s rarely missed a game, and the Belgian has taken everything in his stride.

It’s clear that he’s improving each week too, and although the defence isn’t a complete article, he’s offering himself as something more than an option.

Speaking to TeleLombardia in the mixed zone, De Winter offered his views on the performance and the balance for the future.

“Today we played as a team,” as MilanNews relays, “I’m really happy we won this match. We knew we could win, and we did.”

Did you expect Inter to have so few attackers?

“When we want to and we’re all focused, we can really do well: I think you can feel that in the group too.”

Cardinale came out crying: he said you are winners…

“It’s beautiful, you can feel these games. Even the stadium, you can feel the emotion on the pitch.”

“We have to try to be united every game, to do things right. If we do that, we’ll be really strong, but you have to confirm that in every game.”

#1827. Manchester United XI vs Roma: Starting lineup, confirmed team news, injury latest for Champions League today

Manchester United are still without Patrick Dorgu for their Champions League showdown against Roma.

There had been a hope that Dorgu could help solve the Red Devils’ left-back problems after the versatile winger returned to team training on Monday.

Michael Carrick, the under-fire head coach, confirmed to the media that while the former Lecce man had made a comeback, he would not be involved in the league phase tie.

"It was his first day with the group, great to have him back, but he won't be involved tomorrow,” Carrick said. “We'll see how he progresses for the week [ahead]."

As such, it means that United are once again hamstrung in that position, with Luke Shaw also sidelined with a muscle problem.

Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui have deputised from right-back in recent matches, with central defender Leny Yoro coming in as a makeshift right-sided full-back. Ayden Heaven is in at centre-back, with Dalot at left-back tonight.

Further forward, the Red Devils are still without Marcus Rashford, who remains sidelined with a niggling hip issue that kept him out of the heavy defeats by Como and Bournemouth, while he was not fit enough to face Chelsea either. He has not since returned to training, and will not feature here.

Benjamin Sesko is a longer-term absentee as the Slovenian continues his recovery from a shin problem that curtailed his debut campaign and stunted his start to this season.

It therefore leaves Carrick relatively short of options for the visit of Roma, but he has Kobbie Mainoo to call upon in the engine room after the academy graduate returned to training ahead of the trip to Chelsea, and he was introduced as a substitute at Stamford Bridge.

The England international comes into the starting lineup here.

Summer arrivals Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba have all been rotated in recent weeks as Carrick looks to experiment in a bid to save his job, but it is the latter who partners Mainoo.

#1826. Cristiano Ronaldo hits HAT-TRICK in Al-Nassr's victory - and Portugal star, 41, could have had FIVE after having two ruled out as he closes in on 1,000-goal milestone

Published: 18:16 EDT, 29 October 2026 | Updated: 18:17 EDT, 29 October 2026

Cristiano Ronaldo has edged closer to the 1,000-goal mark after scoring a hat-trick in Al Nassr's 5-3 win over Al Kholood.

The 41-year-old Portugal star scored all three within 15 second-half minutes, finding the back of the net in the 66th, 72nd and 81st minutes to seal all three points at Alawwal Park on Thursday.

Ronaldo's treble has taken him to 985 career goals as he edges nail-bitingly close to the ultimate milestone that he has been chasing for many years, since breaking the record for top goalscorer in football history in 2021.

Addressing the target with his former team-mate Rio Ferdinand in 2024, Ronaldo said: 'I want to reach 1,000 goals. If I don't have any injuries, this for me is the most important (thing), I want that.

'For me, the best mark that I can have in football is to reach, first, 900 goals. After, my challenge is to be at 1,000 goals.'

Despite surpassing Josef Bican five years ago as the all-time top goalscorer for club and country, that number is contested due to a lack of data from some historical records.

Ronaldo's treble has taken him to 985 career goals as he edges nail-bitingly close to the ultimate milestone that he has been chasing for many years

Last week, Ronaldo became football's first multi-billionaire after the veteran forward raked in £225million this year, according to Forbes (source: cristiano/Instagram)

Brazil legend Pele, for example, is recognised by Guinness World Records as having scored 1,279 career goals in 1,363 games, though many of those matches were exhibitions. FIFA lists Pele's total at 767 career goals.

Lionel Messi, meanwhile, has continued to remain hot on Ronaldo's heels, and is the next player directly behind him with 936.

Ronaldo won consecutive Saudi Pro League Golden Boots in 2023-24 and 2024-25. He finished third in last season's scoring race with 28 goals.

Of his 985 official goals, a whopping 450 came during his nine-year spell at Real, while he netted 145 for Manchester United, 146 for his country Portugal, 101 for Juventus, 138 for current club Al-Nassr and five at Sporting Lisbon.

Last week, Ronaldo became football's first multi-billionaire after the veteran forward raked in £225million this year, according to Forbes.

Ronaldo reportedly passed the $2billion mark in career earnings earlier this year, just six years after he was the first footballer to surpass $1billion.

Ronaldo's status comes as he again topped Forbes' football rich list, aided by a lucrative salary at Saudi Arabian side Al-Nassr which is estimated at £488,000-per-day.

Forbes has determined that Ronaldo has also earned £42million off the pitch over the course of the year, which has come via endorsements and his business ventures.

Ronaldo reportedly passed the $2billion mark in career earnings earlier this year (source: cristiano/Instagram)

Ronaldo's off the pitch earnings alone would surpass the total earnings of all but four of his peers.

Confirmation of Ronaldo's continued position at the top of the rich list comes just days after he was fined a measly £215 by Portugal for walking out of their national team during the recent international window.

Ronaldo is joined in the top two by his longtime rival Messi, with the pair occupying the highest two positions for the 12th time in the last 13 years.

Inter Miami star Messi is estimated to have earned £109million over the past year and is expected to soon join Ronaldo in passing the $2billion career earnings milestone.

#1825. Ferdinand predicts selection headache for Arteta with Saliba return and Konsa form

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Rio Ferdinand believes Arsenal defender Ezri Konsa has given Mikel Arteta "some big decisions to make and big headaches" ahead of William Saliba's return.

Konsa joined Arsenal this summer from Aston Villa for a reported £55m and was thrown into the starting line-up after injuries to Saliba and Cristhian Mosquera.

Saliba is yet to feature for the Gunners this season after suffering a back injury in France's World Cup semi-final defeat to Spain in July, but has recently returned to training.

The Frenchman was spotted in training ahead of Arsenal's Champions League encounter with Slavia Prague on Wednesday.

However, Konsa has impressed in Saliba's absence, highlighted by his display during Arsenal's win over Liverpool on Sunday, when the England international led his side in duels won (8/9), tackles won (4/5) and clearances (eight).

Among Arsenal defenders this season, Konsa has won the joint-most tackles (nine) and most possessions (40), as well as winning the second-most duels (54), aerial duels (19) and recording the second-most interceptions (10), trailing Gabriel Magalhaes in all three categories.

Ferdinand praised the impact of Konsa and felt Manchester United should have gone in for the defender in the summer.

"I think William Saliba is one of those guys that you have to find room for in the team," Ferdinand said on his YouTube channel. "He's that good, he's top.

"I wouldn't be surprised if Konsa goes back to right-back once Saliba comes back. I wouldn't be surprised because Konsa is top. He's a top, top player and another one I thought Manchester United should have got because he's a top player.

"He's giving Mikel Arteta some big decisions to make and big headaches because he's slipped in seamlessly and put in some big performances. What a signing he's been for Arsenal."

#1824. “I can’t change it” – Chivu looks back after three derby defeats to Milan

After last night’s win against Inter, AC Milan have now gone eight games without a defeat in the Derby della Madonnina.

In years gone by, the derby was a result to skip over for Milan. It was a defeat waiting to happen and it seemingly couldn’t be changed and then it flipped. Matteo Gabbia’s goal stopped the streak and in turn, it started a new one.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The Rossoneri entered last night’s game with a run of seven unbeaten and they finished the night with eight unbeaten and a fourth consecutive win. It’s a first in itself for more than 50 years, which is telling.

It’s a result which brought Gerry Cardinale to tears and it’s clear that something has really clicked at San Siro, as the player ratings showed.

Speaking at a press conference after the game, as relayed by MilanNews, the Inter coach spoke about several things, including his unfavourable record in the Derby della Madonnina.

“Compared to last year, there’s something to note about our approach to matches: the superficiality and casualness with which we handle certain situations, where we lack a bit of grit, a bit of determination, a bit of danger perception. But we need to rediscover them.

“We need to be aware that right now, despite a few more points than last year, we’ve lost something that absolutely needs to be rediscovered.”

“I couldn’t, because the forwards have had some problems in the last few days. Bonny only made himself available on the last day after two days with a fever of 39°C and severe nausea and vomiting, so we were forced to find a solution, to make a virtue of necessity, changing the system a bit.

“We knew that, in this type of match, it would be the right thing to have pace on the wings with Spence and Carlos and attack the line a bit more, as well as looking for depth in space with Diouf operating under the striker, looking for both him and Sucic between the lines.

“Unfortunately, sometimes things don’t work out, but, I repeat, we were forced to change.”

“It’s too easy to talk now that Lautaro is injured and the other two forwards aren’t feeling well. These things happen, fortunately not often. We’ll make some assessments, but we’re still happy with our four forwards, in addition to what Lavelli gives us, what Mosconi gives us, and whoever we bring in from the Under 23s.

“But, I repeat, it’s too easy to bring these things up at a time when two forwards aren’t at their best and the third is injured.”

Is there something mental that comes into play in the derby?

“There’s always something mental, I think, and history teaches us this, when you get to play another season after winning.

“So, let’s try not to throw everything away and try to rediscover some determination, some humility in doing certain things, starting with myself, because I’m primarily responsible for everything we do.

“We shouldn’t throw everything away because we’ve reached the tenth matchday and this is the first game we’ve lost. We’ve got 25 points, and last year we’d got fewer, but we’ve always been able to react, we’ve always kept our feet on the ground and our heads down to build a strong season.

“That’s what we’d like to do again this year, because we have this desire and this ambition to have another strong season; we just need to find the way to build it again.”

#1822. Man Utd impress in draw against PSG but injury worries mount

Michael Carrick said he had to be careful with Mason Mount after the England midfielder handed Manchester United an injury scare in their friendly draw with Paris St Germain.

Mount has had a torrid time with injuries since signing from Chelsea in a £55m-deal three years ago, starting only 25 Premier League games for United in that time.

The 27-year-old has been successfully deployed by Carrick in a central midfield role during pre-season, leading to speculation that United may not make another expected signing in that department.

But Mount played only 18 minutes of Saturday’s 1-1 draw against the European champions in Gothenburg before being replaced by Scotland international Tyler Fletcher.

“He [Mount] got kicked. We just wanted to be careful and look after him,” Carrick, the United head coach, told reporters in Sweden.

“We’ve been lucky with injuries so far, so we wanted to be careful.”

Post-match video footage showed Mount walking freely on to the United bus without the aid of a protective boot or knee support.

Michael Carrick told VG Mason Mount was taken off as a precaution. Looked OK leaving stadium. pic.twitter.com/Uo0fBtgpAl

United went behind within two minutes at the Ullevi Stadium when Liverpool target Ibrahim Mbaye punished slack marking to put PSG ahead.

Bryan Mbeumo fired United level after 32 minutes following good work from Amad Diallo, the Cameroon forward’s third goal in two games after his match-winning double against Atletico Madrid.

United meet Leeds in a Dublin friendly on Wednesday before coming up against AC Milan and their former manager Ruben Amorim next Saturday.

United open their Premier League campaign at Hull on August 22.

“It was good game. PSG is good so we had to keep building fitness. I am happy to have other [players] back and we have to keep going.”

“It’s good for me. I enjoyed it. We need to build fitness, we have a big season ahead.”

“It’s a good game PSG are tough to beat and we got a draw and now think about the next game [against Leeds in Dublin].”

“We have two more games against Leeds a and Milan. We need to have big season and hope to win a trophy.”

All over in Gothenburg and it’s been a good match for Michael Carrick’s team. They looked sharper and quicker than their win over Atletico Madrid last week (what the manager wanted) and things are moving in the right direction. Two things to worry about, however, were the early exits of Mason Mount and Tom Heaton with injuries. They’ll especially hope the Mount knock isn’t anything mid or long term.

Nearly done and it’s been a good run out for United. They’ve looked the better, sharper side and, if anything, deserve to win. In mitigation, this is United fourth pre-season game to PSG’s second...

Fernandes has one thing on his mind when he gets the ball 25 yards out in the centre of the park - a shot. He unleashes the attempt, destined for the bottom-left corner, forcing Longoni, the sub goalkeeper, into a good save.

Two chances for United in quick succession. A lovely ball from the middle of the park by Zirkzee finds Dalot on the right. He chips the ball to the back post where one of the Fletchers (sorry, I am not sure which) heads for goal. His attempt is blocked and the ball, ultimately, falls at the feet of Lacey whose shot is blazed high over the bar.

There have been plenty of good things for Carrick to take from this match. The passing, while not of the standard of a cut-and-thrust Premier League match, has been good for the time of year, and there have been enough flashes of brilliance/class/invention etc to suggest that pre-season is moving in the right direction.

Lovely bit of play by United. A great pass with the outside of the boot from the inside-left channel by Tielemans finds Fernandes who plays a sidefooted shot that goes just wide.

Tielemans’s first bit of brilliance from the Belgian there.

Both sides losing possession a fair bit at the moment. Strong pre-season vibes right now.

Maguire has had a good game. He’s played a number of long passes from the back and looked assured. This time he’s up in the PSG half and decides to have a pop - his shot testing Safanov, who saves well.

Had there been VAR Safanov might have had something to answer for...he may have beaten Zirkzee to the ball but he flew in the air and jurt the United man in the process.

Anwway, there’s no VAR (hurrah, for those of you who consider it a modern-day evil) and it doesn’t matter.

Chance for United to go ahead and it comes from two things. (i) A long, hopeful ball from Fernandes that looks for Zirkzee (ii) Safanov rushing off his line and into no-man’s land. The ball comes loose and Jack Fletcher, instead of having a go at goal, with the keeper on the ground and out of the game, passes to Lacey whose shot is wide.

Tyler Fletcher loses the ball near the United half and it, ultimately, results in a PSG corner. From the set piece United defend well and snuff out all hint of danger.

PSG seeing more of the ball at the moment. They work the ball to the right and Amass brings down Mbaye.

From the resulting free-kick, in the final third, the French side whip in the ball but Mee is up ot the challenge and come to collect well.

Santos, Mbeumo, Shaw, Amad, Lacey are off

Fernandes, Jack Feltcher, Zirkzee and Amass are on.

A raft of changes for PSG sees Marquinhos and João Neves, among others, come on. More like it, in terms of first-team ‘names’, on the pitch for the European Cup champions.

United on top in this half, as they were in the first.

The paces quickens and the game is much better for it. Mbuemo drives toward the PSG box, he cuts inside from the right before unleashing a shot that is bound for the back of the net before a fine one-handed save by Safanov. Credit, too, for Maguire whose long ball from the back found Mbuemo brilliantly. Promising...

Lacey tries to play in Dorgu on the left but he’s asking too much of his team-mate. Wonder when the expected raft of changes will take place?

Slow start to the second half. This is very much pre-season-friendly pace.

Having seen Mount limp off in the first half, there’s more worry at the start of the second and Heaton is force off with what looks like a hamstrung injury. He dashed off his line to clear a ball and in doing so has tweaked something. Mee replaces him.

Back under way Gothenburg - there have been a number of changes and will bring them to you once I’ve worked out who has come on and who they’ve replaced.

A world record that still stands...(this was back in 1995).

And that is it for the first 45 minutes. PSG took the early lead, but from that moment on United have been the better side and deservedly are level through Mbueno’s goal.

There will be one minute of added time at the end of what has been a good first half for Man Utd.

Amad has a go from outside the box forcing the save from Safanov. He’s such a live wire and one of the best in his position in the top flight. Him or Antony? No contest, strange it took United a while to work that one out.

Yet more good work from the underrated Amad. He again closes down well on the right before winning back possession and cutting the ball back for Lacey. To think he was starring for Sunderland in the Championship while Antony was starting for United...

United have been the better side since conceding earlier and, as if to illustrate my point, as I typed that an Mbuemo free-kick is well saved by Safanov. That was heading for the top-right bin.

Great work on the left by Dorgu and Shaw ends with the latter chipping the ball to the back post where Amad is lurking with intent. The Ivorian looks to head the ball home, but before he can get anything on it it looks as though he’s pushed in the back. United players are sure it’s a penalty but, more importantly, the referee doesn’t.

Amad does brilliantly, winning the ball off Koukaba in the final third, from there he scampers toward the box before playing in Mbuemo who takes one touch before firing in a shot into the bottom right corner of the net.

Free-kick for PSG on the right, near the final third. The ball comes in and it’s straight into the arms of Heaton in the United goal.

Kvaratskhelia, not seen much of him so far, runs into the box, but Amad does well to usher him back out.

The match is pedestrian at the moment, but as I type that, Dorgu, yep, him again, drives down the left and puts in a good cross that is well intercepted by Safanov in the PSG goal.

United continue to see more of the ball, Dorgu’s seeing more of it than most. But, no chances really fashioned, still, plenty of time to go.

Worry for United having to sub off Mount. It looks as though he took a knock to a foot and Carrick and co will hope it’s not a long-term injury. Mount, who’s had a good pre-season, has been replaced by Fletcher, son of Darren.

Foul on Mazraoui results in two things. The Mount has to come off, and, United have a free-kick on the edge of the PSG area.

From the set-piece Mbuemo has a go and it’s a regulation save from Safonov in the PSG goal.

Heaven loses possession in the middle of the park and from there it’s like the parting of the Red Sea as PSG have a three-on-one. Mbaye gets the shot in on goal but Andrey Santos covers back brilliantly and does enough to get something on the ball. He’s started both this match and pre-season well.

United are looking half decent on the ball. They’re passing it well and not afraid to switch things around.

A lovely long ball from Maguire finds Dorgo whose lovely first touch takes him into the box before a cut back is intercepted by a PSG man. Promising signs though for Carrick’s men.

United seeing more of the ball at the moment. They’re being patient but cannot fashion an opening and the ball is worked all the way back to Heaton in goal.

Needless to say this is being played at a slowish pace...no blood-and-guts challenges being put in.

Good work down the right sees Amad plays in Shay Lacey who crosses into the box. The ball find shte head of Mbuemo and the ball sails over the bar. Better from United.

United started slowly against Atletico and they’ve done the same here.

Bright start to say the least from the French side. They work the ball left and it’s an easy cross from Dro Fernandez for Mbaye to tap home for the very early lead.

They’re under way in Sweden. United are in their new vibrant red kit and PSG in their blue, red and white kit. Big fan of the French side’s kit, it harks back to the kit they had in the 1990s when the likes of George Weah and David Ginola were entertaining in the capital of France.

Man Utd: Heaton, Mazraoui, Maguire, Heaven, Shaw, Mount, Santos, Dorgu, Lacey, Amad, Mbeumo; Subs: Heath, Mee, Amass, Armer, Dalot, Yoro, Fernandes, J. Fletcher, T. Fletcher, Tielemans, Zirkzee

Paris St-Germain: Safonov, Pacho, Zabarnyi, Koukaba, Boly, Beraldo, Dro, Mayulu, Kvaratskhelia, Ayari, Mbaye; Subs: Marquinhos, Mendes, Lucea, Vitinha, Neves, El Nay, Idder, Drame, Bourdin, Ndjantou, Meite, Longoni, Chevalier

And here’s a famous match that took place there, giving a certain Sir Alex Ferguson his first European trophy.

“Get a bit sharper, get better on the ball, go up a notch.”

“It’s not about today it’s about preparing. Some players have played 90 minutes, some have played three games, some have just come back. So it’s about keeping working on things we’ve been working on.”

“They’re similar to us, but have fewer senior players available . They’ve had a great time and great squad so whoever on the pitch it will be a test.”

A hugely talented player for a number of clubs, including United, who ever really lived up to his early promise.

Good to have you back, lads 🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/3EgkXLqcQm

📃 Le onze de départ pour cette rencontre de préparation face à Manchester United. #PSGMUN pic.twitter.com/LodcDM1Yrm

I expect they’ll make an appearence at some point.

Ready to face PSG in our latest pre-season test ✊

Manchester United continue their Sweden sojourn with match against Paris St-Germain in Gothenburg.

Clearly a clash against the back-to-back Champions League winners is a step up from their previous two pre-season friendlies (victories against Rosenborg and Atletico Madrid), but at the same time this is more a chance for players to get miles in the legs and see how new signings and possibly some young guns fit in.

One of those new signings is Youri Tielemans, and the Belgian international is in line to make his debut after his move from Aston Villa. Other team news is that Bruno Fernandes is back and ready to captain the team.

Michael Carrick has also been boosted by the returns of Matheus Cunha, Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui after their post-World Cup breaks.

Cunha, however, will not play a part in today’s match because of a “minor illness” according to the MUTV website. He is expected to link up with the squad in Ireland, where they face Leeds United at Croke Park, after the match.

This will be Man Utd’s first outing since the 2-1 win over Atletico, a performance and result that pleased Carrick.

“I enjoyed it, I thought there was a lot of good in things that we are looking to improve on,” the United manager said. “Building on what we did for the last seven months, I think there is a lot of good signs for us, it’s never going to be the exact stage we want to be at. But I thought there was really a lot of positives to take out of the game, individual, collectively as a team, senior players looking strong and fit, and the younger players doing really well.

“The spirit and the camaraderie is so important for the team, it’s great to see the boys getting on so naturally and enjoying each other’s company. Collectively we looked strong as a team, which is always the most important thing, and individual performances seeing the young players come on to have an impact.”

#1821. AC Milan and Inter reveal first pictures of new stadium as San Siro replacement unveiled after £543million naming rights deal

Published: 17:49 EDT, 29 October 2026 | Updated: 19:34 EDT, 29 October 2026

Italian giants AC Milan and Inter have detailed first images of their proposed new stadium ahead of demolishing the San Siro.

The two sides have long looked to move on from their iconic home, with plans to destroy it initially put on hold until things got back on track recently.

The teams shared a preview video of the new ground, with the aim of it opening in the 2031-32 season. It is set to be called the Generali Stadium, with naming rights sold to the insurance brand until 2052 for £543million.

Construction won't begin until 2028, and the stadium is set to hold 71,500 fans. It is to feature an X-frame structure and double-curved roof, with the frame to emphasise two curves, with one dedicated to Inter fans and the other to Milan supporters.

The stadium will be two-tiered, and will also be built with the idea of hosting concerts, with more public spaces, green areas and leisure and retail areas to be included.

Milan and Inter had initially planned on starting building in 2027, with plans to demolish the San Siro put into place as far back as 2019.

A new symbol for Milano.A new home for future generations of fans.Generali Stadium 🏟️@GENERALI pic.twitter.com/c7D0827E7T

Inter and AC Milan have revealed images of their proposed new stadium ahead of the demolition of the San Siro

The stadium will l also host concerts, though won't be ready until the 2031-32 season

Two different outside views were shared - one with blue for Inter's games, and one red for AC Milan's games

Construction won't begin until 2028, and the stadium is set to hold 71,500 fans in total

Images shared of the proposed stadium show the ground in all its expected glory in the heart of Milan.

One design showed a hypothetical game between Inter and AC Milan, with giant tifos of both sides shown in the ground.

A mock up of a concert is also presented, with bright lights on show and thousands of fans in the stadium.

The clubs had already announced agreements last year with architectural firms Foster + Partners and Manica to design a new stadium.

Foster + Partners and Manica's projects include Wembley Stadium in London, Chase Center in San Francisco, and Lusail Stadium in Qatar.

Norman Foster and David Manica presented the plans at Thursday's briefing.

'It is always a challenge to design a building that replaces a beloved project,' Manica said. 'And the way I'm thinking about this project and the spirit that we began with from the beginning was: same soul, different building.

'The most important thing that we realized when we designed this project is that the San Siro is a feeling, more than a building, it's a feeling. And everything that we needed to do here was to drive that feeling and carry it into the building.'

There was initially no objection to the plans, but negotiations dragged on and concerns began to rise over the cultural impact of demolishing the ground, which was built more than 100 years ago.

In 2023, it was ruled that the San Siro could not be demolished because it has 'cultural interest'. In 2025, however, the clubs bought the site to build a new ground, which made the decision to demolish the ground possible.

In its initial form the stadium was completed in 1926 but the middle tier, along with the iconic spiral towers, was added in 1955.

The San Siro was supposed to host the Champions League final this season, but was stripped of the right by UEFA after authorities in the Italian city could not offer guarantees that refurbishment work at the stadium and the surrounding area would not affect the match.

The aim is to host matches at Euro 2032, which Italy will co-host with Turkey.

#1819. Prediction: Fenerbahce vs Liverpool

Liverpool will look to maintain their flawless Champions League record when they travel to Istanbul on Wednesday to face a struggling Fenerbahce side at the Sukru Saracoglu Stadium.

The visitors have won all three of their league-phase matches so far, while Fenerbahce remain without a victory and are already under pressure to keep their hopes of reaching the knockout stages alive.

Fenerbahce head into this fixture in a period of uncertainty.

Former Liverpool favourite Dirk Kuyt is currently overseeing the team on an interim basis following Ismail Kartal’s departure, but the former Dutch international has yet to enjoy a winning start to life in the dugout. A 2-1 defeat against Goztepe at the weekend followed a loss to Galatasaray, extending a disappointing run of results.

European form has also been underwhelming. The Turkish side drew with Roma and Slavia Prague before suffering a humiliating 6-0 defeat away to Aston Villa, leaving them with just two points from three games.

Despite those struggles, home form offers some encouragement. Fenerbahce have lost only once in their last five matches in Istanbul and will hope the hostile atmosphere generated by their supporters can unsettle Liverpool.

There are concerns in defence, however. Jayden Oosterwolde and Kojo Peprah Oppong are unavailable, while Nathan Ake faces a race against time to be fit.

Further forward, Romelu Lukaku is expected to lead the line, supported by Mason Greenwood, Irfan Can Kahveci and Oguz Aydin.

Liverpool arrive in Turkey looking to respond immediately after a disappointing setback against Arsenal.

Andoni Iraola’s side saw a five-match winning streak come to an end when the Gunners secured a 1-0 victory at Anfield, but the broader picture remains overwhelmingly positive. The Reds have enjoyed an impressive start under their new manager and remain among the strongest teams in this season’s Champions League.

Victories over Atletico Madrid, LASK Linz and Villarreal have left Liverpool with a perfect nine-point haul from three matches and sitting among the leading teams in the competition.

Away form has been particularly impressive. Liverpool remain unbeaten on their travels this season and have already demonstrated their ability to win in difficult environments.

The visitors also have some injury concerns. Ryan Gravenberch is unavailable after suffering a heel injury, while Giovanni Leoni, Conor Bradley and Jeremie Frimpong remain sidelined.

Alexander Isak could be rested after a busy schedule, potentially opening the door for Lewis Koumas to start in attack. Ronald Araujo is again expected to continue at right-back.

The atmosphere in Istanbul should make life uncomfortable for Liverpool, and Fenerbahce are likely to play with greater intensity than recent results suggest.

However, the difference in form and quality between the sides is difficult to ignore. Liverpool have looked confident and effective in Europe, while Fenerbahce continue to struggle defensively and have yet to produce a convincing Champions League performance.

The hosts should create opportunities in front of their own supporters, but Liverpool’s superior attacking options and overall structure ought to prove decisive.

#1818. Prediction: Celtic vs Besiktas

Celtic will look for its first Europa League point when Besiktas visits Celtic Park on Thursday, November 5. Kickoff in Glasgow is at 8 p.m. local time (9 p.m. CET).

Besiktas has scored nine goals on its way to seven points from three matches. Celtic has conceded nine, and its last two home games give the visiting attack particular reason for encouragement.

Verdict: Besiktas to score at least two goals Best odds: 93/100 Bookmaker: 1xBet

Celtic was a crossbar away from going 2-0 up in its last Europa League game. Mika Baur had scored just after halftime against Celta Vigo, and Liam Scales nearly doubled the lead when he met a Haissem Hassan cross. By the 71st minute, Celtic was behind.

Javi Rodriguez headed in the equalizer and scored again from outside the box three minutes later. The 2-1 defeat against Celta Vigo followed a 3-1 home loss to Ferencvaros and a 4-1 defeat at Benfica.

Six days later, almost the same thing happened against Dundee United. Camilo Duran put Celtic ahead before Zac Sapsford equalized in the 28th minute and Neil Farrugia scored in the 31st. This time Scales rescued a point, but Martin O’Neill had watched another home lead disappear in three minutes.

Sunday’s 2-0 defeat at Falkirk was frustrating for a different reason. Celtic had 24 attempts, put nine on target and hit the post through Duran. Former Celtic goalkeeper Scott Bain had an excellent afternoon, while Falkirk had already done enough to win the match by halftime.

There is enough in those performances to see Celtic scoring on Thursday. The harder question for O’Neill is how to settle his side after it concedes. Besiktas has several players capable of making the next attack count before Celtic regains its shape.

Alistair Johnston is out with a hamstring injury. Colby Donovan started at right back against Falkirk and is the likely choice again. On the opposite side, Kieran Tierney needs assessment after taking a couple of knocks on Sunday.

Jota is ineligible because he was left out of Celtic’s Europa League squad. Yang Hyun-jun is working his way back from a hamstring problem, while Oliver Sorensen’s availability remains uncertain after he missed the trip to Falkirk for family reasons.

Cameron Carter-Vickers returned to the starting lineup on Sunday alongside Scales. Further forward, Baur has scored two of Celtic’s three league-phase goals, and Hassan’s deliveries from the right gave both Duran and Scales chances against Celta.

The Besiktas player with the best reason to look forward to this trip is former Celtic striker Oh Hyeon-gyu. He had a hand in all three goals in the 3-2 win at Hoffenheim, the Turkish club’s only away fixture in the league phase so far.

Oh set up Michael Murillo for the opener. When Hoffenheim equalized, he scored in the 72nd and 79th minutes. Celtic knows what he offers in the box, and his performance in Germany gives Vincenzo Italiano a good reason to use him at some point in Glasgow.

The goals have come from elsewhere, too. Besiktas opened its campaign with a 4-1 victory over Marseille. In the 2-2 draw with Crystal Palace, midfielder Wilfred Ndidi opened the scoring before Junior Olaitan earned a point with a shot from outside the area. Keeping track of the center forward will only solve part of Celtic’s problem.

Sunday’s 2-2 draw at Kasimpasa explains the appeal of backing the visiting attack. Ridvan Yilmaz picked out Leandro Trossard for the opening goal, and Dusan Vlahovic made it 2-0 shortly after halftime. Besiktas still had to settle for a point after conceding an 87th-minute equalizer.

That was the third straight match in which Besiktas scored exactly twice. Only one of those games ended in victory.

Captain Orkun Kokcu remains a doubt with the foot injury he suffered at Hoffenheim. Reports in Turkey suggest Italiano will assess Kokcu in training before deciding whether he can feature. Ndidi and Salih Ozcan started together in midfield at Kasimpasa.

Fabio Miretti is sidelined with a shoulder injury. Center back Umit Akdag is suspended after his red card against Crystal Palace, leaving Emmanuel Agbadou and Emirhan Topcu in contention to continue in front of Alexander Nubel.

Vlahovic and Trossard both strengthened their claims to start with goals on Sunday. Italiano also used Oh alongside Vlahovic for the closing stages, an option if Besiktas needs a goal late on.

Celtic has created enough chances at home to make an outright away win a difficult call. Baur and Duran have both put Celtic ahead at Parkhead in recent weeks, and Besiktas comes into this game after letting a two-goal lead slip.

The stronger bet is on what happens at the other end. Celtic has conceded at least twice in every league-phase fixture, while Besiktas has reached that mark against French, German and English opposition. Even if Vlahovic starts alone up front, Italiano can turn to a striker who scored twice in seven minutes on his last European away trip.

At 93/100, Besiktas to score at least two goals is the pick.

Verdict: Besiktas to score at least two goals Best odds: 93/100 Bookmaker: 1xBet

#1816. Man United consider shock Dominic Calvert-Lewin move as club launch search for new striker after Benjamin Sesko injury blow left them with NO fit centre-forward

Published: 15:44 EDT, 29 October 2026 | Updated: 20:15 EDT, 29 October 2026

Manchester United are exploring the possibility of a move for Leeds striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin as the club looks to strengthen in attack in January.

Daily Mail Sport understands a move is viewed as difficult given the fierce rivalry between the two clubs.

Calvert-Lewin has revitalised his career at Leeds after joining on a free transfer in the summer of 2025, following an injury-plagued end to his time at Everton.

The 29-year-old has scored 20 goals in 49 appearances for Leeds, including five in ten games at the start of this season.

Calvert-Lewin scored against Man United when the two sides played out a 1-1 draw earlier this month.

The forward’s form earned him an England recall during the last international window, ending a five-year absence from the national team set-up.

Man United are exploring a possible move for Leeds United forward Dominic Calvert-Lewin

Calvert-Lewin netted against the Red Devils in a 1-1 draw between the sides earlier this month

Man United are currently without a recognised striker with Benjamin Sesko on the sidelines

Calvert-Lewin, who has started 38 times in his 43 Premier League appearances for Leeds, is currently contracted until 2028.

Man United are currently operating without a recognised striker with Benjamin Sesko having been ruled out until at least January with a shin injury.

The 23-year-old was struggling with the issue at the beginning of the season and saw his game time carefully managed as the club attempted to nurse him back to full fitness but those efforts now appear to have been in vain.

Sesko has not featured for the club since their defeat by Brighton in the Carabao Cup on September 16, when he was substituted in the 66th minute.

He missed all of pre-season with the complaint, which also plagued him last season and resurfaced against Liverpool in May, causing him to miss the final three Premier League games.

The Slovenian, who pulled out of international duty last month, now looks set to be sidelined until the new year, dealing a major blow to United during a difficult run of form and leaving Michael Carrick without a recognised striker.

Cantona's move to Man United was credited as one of Sir Alex Ferguson's most successful moves, with the Frenchman helping to transform his side into title winners.

The maverick star had seen his relationship break down with Leeds boss Howard Wilkinson leading to speculation over a departure.

Leeds chairman Bill Fotherby called his Man United counterpart Martin Edwards to enquire about signing Denis Irwin. After the suggestion was rebuffed by Edwards, Ferguson then asked about Cantona’s availability with a £1.2m deal then being struck.

While initially seen as a risky move, Cantona helped inspire Man United to a first title in 26 years. The Frenchman was part of four title winning sides at Old Trafford and won two FA Cups.

Ferdinand became the most expensive British footballer in history when he completed a £30m move in 2002 after two seasons at Leeds. Ferdinand has claimed he sat in the office of Leeds chairman Peter Ridsdale for six hours to force through the transfer.

The deal came amid growing concerns over Leeds financial situation, which was referenced by Sir Alex Ferguson when the transfer was completed.

‘A transfer like this has to be difficult. Leeds are a big club and our fiercest rivals, and he had four years left on his contract,’ Ferguson said. ‘We were hopeful because of Leeds' financial position. I think Peter Ridsdale has admitted that. Most importantly, Rio wanted to come here and this contributed to the deal.’

Ferdinand would go on to win six Premier League titles, the Champions League and two League Cups during his time with the Red Devils.

Life-long Leeds fan Smith moved to Old Trafford in a deal worth £7million, with Danny Pugh going the opposite way.

Smith opted to make the move following Leeds relegation to the Championship, which had left him in tears on the final day of the season. Smith's move angered Leeds fans having previously declared he would never play for Man United.

The move, however, had helped Leeds amid the club's financial turmoil with Smith also waving a fee that was owed to him.

Sir Alex Ferguson hailed Smith, stating 'I have never been more impressed with a young player, his desire to play for Manchester United is fantastic'.

Smith career at Man United was heavily impacted by a broken leg and dislocated ankle he suffered in an FA Cup tie against Liverpool. He ultimately played 93 times for Man United, scoring 12 times, before moving to Newcastle.

Darlow is the most recent player to move between the two clubs, with the goalkeeper rejected a new deal at Leeds in favour of a move to Old Trafford.

He had been Leeds first choice goalkeeper for much of last season but is now back-up to Senne Lammens at United. Darlow made his debut in Man United's Carabao Cup defeat by Brighton.

When his summer move was confirmed, Leeds issued a 309-word statement but declined to name where Darlow had moved, instead stating he 'wished to explore a different challenge'.

Right winger Bryan Mbeumo has been filling in at No9, starting their last five games there in all competitions, with Michael Carrick having lost faith in Dutchman Joshua Zirkzee.

The decades-old rivalry between the clubs was highlighted in the summer when goalkeeper Karl Darlow became the first player to join Man United from Leeds since Alan Smith in 2004.

Leeds refused to mention Man United in a statement confirming Darlow's departure at the end of his contract, with the club writing that he had 'wished to explore a different challenge'.

Eric Cantona and Rio Ferdinand are among the most famous examples of star names to swap Leeds for the Red Devils.

Daniel James moved from Man United to Leeds in a £25million transfer back in 2021, while Cameron Borthwick-Jackson was part of a rare loan deal between the sides in 2017 when Leeds were in the Championship.

#1815. Derby County vs Norwich City - prediction, team news, lineups

By Calum Burrowes | 02 Nov 2026 14:59, Last updated: 02 Nov 2026 16:56

Looking to claim just their second win of the season, Derby County welcome Norwich City to Pride Park on Tuesday night in desperate need of a positive result to kick-start their Championship campaign.

The Rams suffered their eighth league defeat of the season after being thrashed 4-1 by Millwall in London at the weekend, while the Canaries ended their three-match losing streak at home with a 3-2 victory over fellow strugglers Watford.

After finishing just four points outside the playoff places last season, a position that would have secured them a spot in the top six this time around, many expected Derby County to build on their progress under John Eustace and mount a more serious challenge for promotion back to the Premier League.

However, after 13 matches of the 2026-27 campaign, only one side has collected fewer points than the Rams, with the Derbyshire outfit sitting 23rd on seven points and having failed to win in more than two months.

Eustace's side travelled to The Den knowing they would face a difficult task against a Millwall team now just four points outside the top eight, but few would have anticipated such a disastrous start, with Derby finding themselves three goals down after just 17 minutes following a brace from Kyrell Lisbie.

The 4-1 loss was their third defeat in four matches, with increasing questions now being asked about Eustace's future as he prepares to take charge of his 78th game as Derby manager on Tuesday, hoping to get his side back on track before their situation becomes even more difficult.

Such has been the nature of their poor start to the campaign that even a victory on Tuesday night would not be enough to lift Derby out of the relegation zone.

As for Norwich City, they make the trip to Pride Park having endured a similarly disappointing start to the season, but they appear to have turned a corner after securing back-to-back victories over Charlton Athletic and Watford.

Heading into their 12th Championship fixture, the Canaries sat 21st and just three points above Derby, but six points from their last two matches have lifted Philippe Clement's side to 15th, giving them a six-point cushion over the relegation zone.

Saturday's clash with struggling Watford looked set to bring another disappointing result at Carrow Road after Norwich fell two goals behind inside the opening 27 minutes, but a determined second-half performance provided further signs of a revival and eased the growing pressure on their Belgian head coach.

Goals from Ben Chrisene, Anthony Musaba and Paris Maghoma completed a remarkable comeback, moving Norwich closer to the playoff places than the bottom three and helping to restore a more positive atmosphere around the club.

Their previous victory over the Addicks had ended a six-match losing streak, while the weekend's success against the Hornets was their first home win in three outings, giving the Canaries renewed confidence ahead of their 14th match of the campaign.

Norwich make the trip to Derby for the first time in more than 12 months, having suffered a 1-0 defeat at Pride Park last season before appointing Clement in the following weeks.

Given Derby's dismal run of form, Eustace may have been considering changes regardless, but further injury problems mean he will have even fewer options available for Tuesday's encounter.

David Ozoh was forced off in the first half against Millwall with a muscle injury and is expected to miss this match, with Alex Mowatt the most likely candidate to replace him in midfield.

The injured midfielder will join Craig Forsyth, Derry Murkin, Charlie Taylor, Eiran Cashin and Sondre Langas on the sidelines.

As for Norwich, they will be without Papa Amadou Diallo, Ali Ahmed and Mohamed Toure for the midweek encounter, but Clement could name the same starting XI that completed the comeback against Watford.

With Australian forward Toure sidelined since the end of September, Mathias Kvistgaarden is expected to continue leading the line in his absence as he looks to add to the three Championship goals he has scored this season.

W. Zetterstrom; Johnston, Nyambe, Robinson, Hedges; Mowatt, Clark; Brewster, Szmodics, Meister; Morris

Grimshaw; Stacey, McConville, Cordoba, Chrisene; Wright, Field; Brooks, Maghoma, Musaba; Kvistgaarden

Norwich head to Pride Park as favourites after putting their poor start behind them with successive victories, particularly given the struggles of a Derby side who have won just once all season.

However, with the Rams desperate to turn things around and the visitors still looking to build consistency, we expect a closely contested encounter in which the spoils are shared.

#1814. Atlético Madrid contacts Stefan Džodić’s representatives

Atlético Madrid has spoken to Stefan Džodić’s representatives about a possible move from Almería in the summer of 2027, according to Matteo Moretto of Marca. The 21-year-old midfielder made his senior debut for Serbia last month.

Moretto puts Džodić’s release clause at €40 million and reports that Atlético intends to continue the discussions over the coming months. The two clubs have done business before: Atlético signed right back Marc Pubill from Almería in July 2025. Moretto believes that relationship could help them negotiate a fee below the clause.

Džodić moved to Almería that same summer on a free transfer from Montpellier. Almería recruited him as a holding midfielder who could also play at center back. At his presentation, he was asked whether he expected to play for the first team or the reserves. He went on to make 33 regular-season league appearances and play in all four of Almería’s promotion playoff games in his first year in Spain.

He started six of the first eight league fixtures this season. His absence for the other two, against Mallorca and Burgos, coincided with a call-up from Serbia coach Veljko Paunović, who handed him his debut against Germany in Munich on October 1.

A week later, Almería announced that Džodić had signed a two-year extension through June 2032. Even if Atlético waits until next summer, Almería will still have five years left on his contract.
