#1813. Chelsea’s feisty friendly ends in penalty shoot-out confusion

Chelsea’s Far East tour ended in farce and confusion with players waiting around for a penalty shoot-out that never happened.

The chaos came at the end of a hard-earned, bad-tempered draw against Malaysian champions Johor Darul Ta’zim, with an own-goal in the 89th minute sparring the west London side’s blushes.

That goal also was supposed to set up penalties. But after minutes of waiting around – and Kevin Campello, Chelsea’s head of first-team operations, saying “it’s written in the contract” – the players walked off the pitch.

That confusion ended a feisty affair in which tensions threatened to boil over and that, at certain points, paid little attention to the “friendly” aspect of the clash with seven yellow cards shown. At one point the visitors’ new set-piece coach Austin MacPhee exchanged angry words with some of Johor’s coaching staff. The CFC TV commentary team suggested that the spot-kicks were abandoned because of the match’s heated atmosphere.

Austin MacPhee was ready to throw hands😂 pic.twitter.com/CFDgTOwmxE

Having played just 24 hours earlier in Jakarta – a 3-0 win over AC Milan – it was no surprise to see Xabi Alonso name a fresh XI, a mixture of players who may well be offloaded before the end of the transfer window, those needing to prove themselves, and youngsters given much-needed game time.

And considering Johor are one game away from setting a new world record of 109 matches unbeaten in the top flight – a run that would surpass the current mark set by Ivorian side Asec Mimosas in the early 1990s – it was also no shock to see the Malaysian team offer a stern, pre-season test for the west Londoners.

After a good start Chelsea were second best in a first half in which Johor should have been at least two goals to the good. The Malaysian champions controlled the first 45 minutes and were 1-0 up after 14 minutes – a low cross from the left side-footed home by Arif Aiman.

The hosts gave the young, inexperienced Chelsea backline a torrid time, especially on the flanks and Óscar Arribas was guilty of not capitalising on a great chance to double Johor’s lead, his shot after cutting in from the right going wide.

While they looked vulnerable at the back, Chelsea also struggled to keep possession in attack. But they got an equaliser they scarcely deserved after Liam Delap was manhandled to the ground in the box by Kevin Medina. The striker, who may well leave Stamford Bridge before the transfer window slams shut, fired home the spot-kick allowing the visitors to go into the break on level terms.

For the most part, the second half followed a similar pattern to the first – Jofor having the better chances, while tensions on the pitch continued to run high.

It was, however, Chelsea who took the lead after the break, Delap once again scoring from the spot, this time after Jamie Gittens was brought down in the area.

Johor, though, kept on creating, thanks in part to a fairly porous visitors’ backline, and levelled through a deflected Arribas free kick, before going 3-2 up thanks thanks to a well-taken Bérgson strike.

Had it stayed that way Chelsea could have had few complaints. But as the clock approached 90 minutes, the visitors had one last attack. Mykhailo Mudryk, just on as a substitute, delivered a cross from the left that Antonio Glauder could only steer into his own net. That was supposed to set up the penalty shoot-out that did not take place and the chance for one of the sides to claim a hollow victory.

Considering a raft of changes and that fact this was far from the first XI, it is hard to know what to make of this. But among the positive things Alonso could take from the game was the impressive form of Nicolas Jackson and good centre-forward play of Delap. The negative was, however, a poor defensive display.

Chelsea return to Stamford Bridge on Saturday for their last pre-season friendly, against Real Sociedad, before the Premier League season starts away at local rivals Fulham on August 24.

Johor Darul Ta’zim: Syihan Hazmi; Arribas, Israfilov (Carlos Akapo 82), Medina, Antonio Glauder, Silva (La’Vere Corbin-Ong 89); Arif Aiman, Petrovic, Méndez (Nené 78), Marcos Guilherme (Bérgson); Zahedi (Stoichkov 62). Substitutes: Abad, Davies, Hidalgo, Nahuel Leiva, Lowry, Mohamadou Sumareh, Stuart Wilkin.Booked: Israfilov, Antonio Glauder, Silva.Goals: Arif Aiman (14), Arribas (65), Bérgson (86).Chelsea: Sharman-Lowe (Slolina 46); Subuloye, Adarabioyo, Anselmino (Watson 29); Geovany Quenda, Dario Essugo, Nicoll-Jazuli, Gittens (Mudryk 87); Estêvão, Delap, Jacskon (Satpaev 86). Substitutes: Curd, Diakite, Kavuma-McQueen, Sarr, Walsh.Booked: Estêvão, Delap, Jackson, Geovany Quenda, Watson.Goals: Delap (42 pen, 62 pen), Antonio Glauder (89 og).

There will NOT be a penalty shootout. No one is quite sure why.

Anyway, that was an entertaining draw, plenty of good things for Chelsea (the play of Delap and Jackson) as well as worrying signs (open and vulnerable at the back).

The commentators on CFC TV are now not so sure!

That was an entertaining pre-season friendly. There was a bit of niggle and that added to the action.

There will be penalties, apparently, if it stays the same score...

Will there be a late winner? There will be four minutes of added time.

Mudryk just on picks up the ball on the left and, with four Chelsea players in the box, crosses into the danger area. It’s a good ball and asks too many questions of the hosts as Glauder diverts the ball into his own net.

It’s what the host have, on the balance of play, deserved, but it’s a gift from Chelsea. Essugo loses the ball in the final third and Bergson, on as sub pick it put driving at the box before hitting a low shot from outside the area, the ball nestling in the left corner of the net.

Chelsea have been better this half than the first 45, they’ve been able to control the pace of the game well since the break.

The pace has slowed down since the break, Chelsea seeing more of the ball. They work it right before Watson loses possession on the edge of the area.

The referee clearly forgot about the hydration break and the two teams are having a belated one now. Delightful...

I reckon there’s another goal left in this match. It’s been entertaining fare and the hosts have given as good as they’ve got, if not more.

This has been a lively match, better than most run-of-the-mill pre-season friendlies. Chelsea seeing a fair bit of possession at the moment, can they fashion a chance?

Yes they can. But it’s a longish shot from Gittens that is easily saved by Hamzi in the JDT goal.

More niggle in this match that hasn’t really had many tough challenges. After a few handbags the referee takes control and the argy bargy peters out.

It’s the least the hosts deserve. They have a free-kick 25 yards out, Arribas takes it with his right it’s at the wall but in turning away from the ball Delap deflects it into the far-right corner giving Slonina no chance.

Fluky goal but the hosts have deserved their bit of luck.

Delap again with the goal, this time he goes low, but still to the keeper’s right.

Penalty for Chelsea. Gittens cuts back in the box onto his right and is clipped by the defender. Clear-cut penalty.

Half-chance for Delap on the edge of the area. He playes a one-two with Jackson before opening up his body and letting fly, the shot going well wide.

Another good chance for the hosts and it’s not shock to write that it’s come from the industry of Arribas on the right. He fires in a low cross that evades everyone in the box.

Estevao goes down in the box, it looks as though it could well be a penalty but the referee waves play on. The Brazilian is the shown a yellow card for possibly lashing out having not got the decision he wanted.

The hosts have asserted themselves well this half, in much the same way as they did in the first 45 minutes.

Another good chance for the hosts and again it’s all too easy as Zahedi is one-on-one with the keeper. The striker, however, dithers a bit too long and Slonina makes a fine save. JDT have had plenty of chances to add to their sole goal...

Chelsea have had a ragged start to this half.

Good work from JDT who keep the ball well in midfield before a throughball is played to the on-rushing Zahedi but Slonina comes out well.

They’re back under way in Johor, and there’s an early chance for Jackson who gets the ball in the box, but the ball gets stuck underneath him and he cannot get in a good attempt in on goal.

And that is the last action of an entertaining half. Chelsea started well before the hosts opened the scoring. JDT then took control of the half and should, if truth be told, have extended their lead. But Delap did well to earn the penalty that he subsequently scored and should have made it 2-1 with the last kick of the 45.

Worrying signs at the back, however, for Alonso. Will Chelsea go to four at the back after the break?

The answer to that question (see last post) was so very nearly yes...

Jackson plays in a peach of a through ball with the outside of his right foot, Delap is one-on-one with the keeper and looks for all the world as though he has to score. BUT he scuffs his shot wide.

There will be three minutes of added time. Can Chelsea head into the break with an unexpected lead?

Free-kick for Chelsea on the JDT byline. The ball is put deep into the box, it’s headed back by Tosin before the ball is blazed over the bar.

A minute later Tosin then let’s fly form 25 yards, the ball goes well over the bar.

The hosts should have been more than 1-0 to the good and now they’re drawing. Goals change matches...

Having won the penalty Delap fires the spotkick home, sending the keeper the the wrong way.

Penalty to Chelsea and it’s all thanks to good centre-forward play by Delap. He gets the ball in the box and Medina manhands him to the ground. The referee doesn’t hesitate before pointing to the spot.

Chelsea have struggled to create anything since the opening 15 minutes. They have no control at the front and none at the back currently.

As I type that JDT have another good chance to turn the 1-0 lead into a 2-0 lead. Arribas, whose been a menace all game, dances toward the Chelsea box before delaying the pass too long.

JDT are finding a lot of joy on the flanks, there are three at the back for Chelsea and on the outside are two youngsters. The hosts are working the space well.

Yet again Chelsea are made to look decidedly average. A simple ball over the top on the right opens up the visitors’ defence and Arribas is in on goal, he cuts in and lets fly with his left peg, the shot going wide.

That should have been 2-0 to the Malaysian powerhouses.

Worrying signs for Chelsea who have struggled to keep possession up top and looked vulnerable at the back.

Yet more good work from JDT who are being given space by Chelsea. Marcos Guilherme slaloms into the west Londoners’ box and Tosin again doesn’t look the most assured but the JDT player cuts the ball back and the visitors can clear the danger.

Another good attack from the hosts who get in a shot in on goal, it’s deflected and loops into the grateful arms of Sharman-Lowe in the Chelsea goal.

There’s a break in play with Anselmino down and suffering what looks like a hamstring injury. He is eventually replaced by Reggie Watson.

Meanwhile, the home fans are in fine voice and waving several HUGE flags.

Yep, everyone’s least favourite part of the World Cup in the U, S of A is back. To be fair it’s humid in Johor so taking on fluids during the first 45 minutes is no bad idea.

There’s a bit of argy-bargy not really what you should get in a ‘friendly’. There hasn’t been a bad chellenge in the match so far so not sure where that came from...

Yet more good work from the hosts, this time it’s down the right, Arribas getting the better of Anselmino before shooting at the near post - the attempt hitting the side netting.

After a lively start Chelsea have been second best.

Poor defending from the visitors there but the chance was well snapped up by JDT.

Lovely break from the hosts. They break down the left at pace, before the ball is threaded through to the back post and Arif Aiman sidefoots into the back of the net with aplomb.

So very nearly an opener for Chelsea. They break at pace thanks to Estevao who drives down the middle before playing in Jackson. The striker cuts in from the left and shoots, the attempt is saved well by Hamzi and Estevao’s follow up is wide. Is a goal coming?

Free-kick for Chelsea some 35 yards out. Too far fro a shot on goal? Of course it is. The ball is floated into the box and the visitors earn a corner.

What can they create from this set piece? ‘Not much’ is the initial answer as the ball is cleared by JDT but Chelsea win possession back and the ball is fed to Estevao on the left, the Brazilian goes for go with his trusty left peg but the bal goes high and wide.

JDT attack down the left, it’s a lovely ball in that forces a fine header to clear the danger from Adarabioyo.

No sooner had I sent that last post than Chelsea break through the middle. The ball is fed through to Delap who gets a left-footed shot in on goal forcing a good save from the JDT keeper Hamzi.

Quiet, low-key start to the match. No real shock there, it is a pre-season friendly.

JDT give the ball away in their half and Chelsea have a half-decent platform to launch an attack from. They cannot fashion a chance and also lose possession.

They’re under way in southern Malaysia, Chelsea are in their vibrant blue and the hosts are wearing a fetching pink number. There was a late change for the visitors, Mamadou Sarr has been replaced by Olutayo Subuloye.

CHELSEA XI TO FACE JOHOR: Sharman-Lowe; Sarr, Tosin, Anselmino; Quenda, Nicoll-Jazuli, Essugo (c), Gittens; Estevao; Jackson, Delap; subs: Slonina, Curd, Subuloye, Diakite, Watson, Mudryk, Walsh, Kavuma-McQueen, Satpayev

...Luis Garcia. The Spaniard has history with Chelsea, remember the ‘ghost goal’?

Arriving for duty! 🫡 pic.twitter.com/M2XEkLC18n

Your Chelsea side today! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/0OvvGVmgpc

A mixture of players who may well be offloaded before the end of the transfer window, those needing to prove themselves, and youngsters you may not have heard of.

Johor Darul Ta’Zim – more commonly known as JDT – are the Man Utd of Malaysia (at least that’s according to a Malaysian friend of mine). In 2013, they were going nowhere and were the dictionary definition of a stagnant club, low on confidence and trophies. That was until the Crown Prince bought the club and, over the next 13 years, transformed it into the powerhouse it is today.

As if to underline JDT’s dominance over Malaysian football they are one game away from the world record unbeaten run in a top flight. The new season of the Malaysian Super League gets under way later this month and should they avoid defeat in their opening match they will extend their unbeaten run - which began in April 2021 - to 109 games and surpass the world record set by Ivorian side Asec Mimosas in the early 1990s.

Chelsea’s pre-season tour of South East Asia ends today with a match against Johor Darul Ta’zim in Malaysia. The clash comes barely 24 hours after the west Londoners beat AC Milan 3-0 in Jakarta, a much-needed win coming on the back of defeats against Juventus and Tottenham.

A fine volley from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to victory in the Indonesian capital.

The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

Alonso’s side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.

Just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

Today, the west London side face Malaysian powerhouses Johor at the Sultan Ibrahim Stadium, more on them later, but considering the tight turnaround from yesterday’s match today’s clash will provide a stern test.

“The idea, with the game against Milan and then one in Johor, was to arrive at this weekend with players not being ready for 90 minutes until now,” Alonso explained after the win in Jakarta.

“We wanted to have a logical progression in their loads; so we had our plan and we’ve stuck to that.

“We have another idea [against Johor]; that was decided yesterday [Friday]. The idea is that many young players were coming to have chances to play tomorrow. If not, we’d have been short, as playing two games in two days is quite intense. So we will need them.”

#1812. Barella admits Inter have changed derby approach in recent years: “We’re too inconsistent”

After the game, Nicolo Barella attempted to lessen the damage of last night’s loss to AC Milan in his post-game press conference.

For Milan, last night was another instance in what is becoming a new norm. After Inter’s streak of derby wins, it’s now the Rossoneri who are enjoying themselves. They’ve won each of their last four meetings and haven’t lost in eight games.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In short, despite all of the managerial changes that have taken place, the Diavolo remain on top when it comes to playing the Nerazzurri.

Of course, last night’s win was also monumental considering what it meant for the Serie A table. Rather than falling 10 points behind, they only sit four points behind Inter and Lazio, who share first.

Speaking at a post-match conference, Barella admitted that Inter are going through a bad cycle in the derbies, but was keen to remember the streak from a few years ago, as MilanNews relayed.

“Certainly, if we talk about this, we’ve been lacking the ideal approach to matches since the start of the year. Right now, it’s a clear criticality for us.

“It’s true that we’ve shown our strength on many occasions, perhaps coming out on top in the second half or whenever we manage to break the deadlock, but it’s clear that not every match goes that way.

“We can’t expect to always repeat the same pattern, especially when we face a packed schedule with matches every three days. Fatigue, both physical and mental, is starting to take its toll, and we need to learn to manage matches better without being forced to keep them in the balance until the ninetieth minute.”

Is there a feeling that, whatever you do, Milan will prevail in derbies?

“Let’s say I’ve also experienced it the other way around. I’ve had a lot of derby wins in a row, so I don’t know if it’s a cyclical thing, but it’s definitely a game we haven’t approached in the best way in recent years, recently.

“There have been derbies where we’ve played well and lost, where we’ve played poorly and maybe drawn, but we’re too inconsistent in derbies, and right now, even in important matches. Even though we won, we still needed to do better.”

Do you still have the fierce desire to prove that you are the strongest?

“Being the strongest is sometimes not enough, because we’ve also been the strongest team, or the one everyone thought was the strongest, but then we didn’t win. So right now, I think we need to focus on something else rather than our strength.

“It’s true that if we look back at the last few games, many goals come from individual errors, and we need to improve on those, each of us, because unfortunately, individual errors work against the team. But as a team, we need to improve a bit in terms of solidity, which is what has always set us apart, what got us to the Champions League final, what helped us win the Scudetto, and perhaps right now we’re not the best version of ourselves. So we need to work on that. We still have the desire to win, for sure, because that’s what keeps us going to the pitch every day and motivates us, but we need to improve.”

#1811. Prediction: AC Milan vs Ferencvaros

AC Milan welcome Ferencvaros to San Siro on Thursday night knowing that anything less than victory could leave their Europa League campaign in serious jeopardy.

While the Italian giants sit precariously near the cutoff line after an inconsistent start to the league phase, Ferencvaros arrive in Milan with a perfect record and growing belief that a place in the top eight is within reach.

Milan’s Europa League campaign has been anything but straightforward.

The Rossoneri began with defeat against Benfica before responding with a commanding 4-0 victory over Salzburg. However, their progress was halted dramatically on matchday three as Bournemouth secured a stunning 3-0 victory, leaving Ruben Amorim’s side with just three points from three matches.

The pressure is now increasing on Milan, who currently occupy one of the final playoff positions and can ill afford another setback.

Domestically, though, there are signs of encouragement. After a disappointing defeat to Bologna, Milan produced one of their best performances of the season by defeating city rivals Inter 3-1 in the Derby della Madonnina. That victory has revived optimism around Amorim’s project and moved the club closer to the leading group in Serie A.

Squad rotation is expected, with several younger players potentially earning opportunities. Alphadjo Cisse is pushing for a starting role after an impressive run of form, while Omari Hutchinson and Davide Bartesaghi may also feature.

Goalkeeper Mike Maignan is suspended following his red card against Bournemouth, meaning Lorenzo Torriani is expected to start.

Injuries continue to affect the hosts, with Fikayo Tomori, Ruben Loftus-Cheek, Samuel Chukwueze, Alexis Saelemaekers and Mattia Gabbia all unavailable.

Ferencvaros have been one of the surprise packages of this season’s Europa League.

The Hungarian champions have collected maximum points from their opening three matches, defeating Celtic, Viktoria Plzen and Torreense to establish themselves among the league phase frontrunners.

Balazs Borbely’s side now sit fourth in the standings and appear well placed to challenge for automatic qualification to the last 16.

Their strong European performances reflect impressive overall form. Across domestic and continental competition, Ferencvaros have suffered only one defeat all season and continue to build momentum. A 2-0 victory over Paks at the weekend ensured they remained firmly in contention for another Hungarian league title.

The visitors possess a growing attacking threat. Kristoffer Zachariassen and Dele Yusuf have both enjoyed productive starts to the Europa League campaign, while Veljko Birmancevic adds pace and creativity in wide areas.

There are only a couple of notable absences. Matus Bero is unavailable in midfield, while Bence Otvos remains out with a long-term knee injury.

Ferencvaros arrive in Italy with every reason to be confident and should make life difficult for a Milan side still searching for consistency in Europe.

However, San Siro remains a formidable venue, and the derby victory over Inter may prove to be a turning point for Amorim’s team. While the visitors are capable of competing for long periods, Milan’s greater individual quality and growing confidence should ultimately make the difference.

Expect a competitive contest, one that the Rossoneri are narrowly favoured to win, but not with a clean sheet.

#1810. Man United transfer news: Borussia Dortmund quartet targeted after 'scouting mission'

By Darren Plant | 02 Nov 2026 15:25

Manchester United are reportedly interested in signing as many as four Borussia Dortmund players, including Serhou Guirassy.

Michael Carrick will continue to fight for his job at Old Trafford on Tuesday evening when United square off against Roma in the Champions League.

Despite Carrick's defiance at a press conference on Monday, the Englishman may be sacked if the Red Devils lose to the Italian giants and Aston Villa on Sunday.

As a result, it is unclear whether Carrick will have any influence on signings planned for the winter transfer window.

According to TEAMtalk, United chiefs are already considering who to target at the midway point of the campaign after a recent trip to Germany.

The report claims that United have already sent scouts to monitor the development of Guirassy, Dortmund's leading marksman.

Guirassy has netted eight times this season, but his contract at the Westfalenstadion is due to expire in 2028.

Not only is the 30-year-old on United's radar, they are also said to be admirers of Daniel Svensson, Jobe Bellingham and Felix Nmecha.

Bellingham and Nmecha, as well as Guirassy, all started Dortmund's 2-2 draw with Bayern Munich last weekend, helping the club stay level on points with their arch rivals in the Bundesliga table.

Svensson has also become a target for United having grown into his role at Dortmund and the English team's desire to strengthen at left-back.

Since his arrival in 2025, the 24-year-old has contributed eight goals and seven assists from 80 appearances in all competitions.

Despite their struggles in central midfield, United are well stocked for options in that area of the pitch, so moves for the likes of Bellingham and Nmecha may be put on the back-burner.

However, Svensson could be viewed as a successor to Luke Shaw, while Guirassy - despite his age - may be seen as someone who can hit the ground running at Old Trafford.

In all cases, however, striking a deal with Dortmund is more likely in the summer than in January.

#1808. AEK Athens vs Real Madrid - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 02 Nov 2026 15:28, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 14:15

Real Madrid will be aiming to continue their 100% start to this season's Champions League league stage when they take on AEK Athens in Athens on Wednesday evening.

Los Blancos are currently fourth in the overall Champions League table, picking up nine points from three matches, while AEK Athens are 29th in the division on three points.

AEK Athens opened their Champions League league stage campaign with a 1-0 victory over LASK Linz, but they have since been on the end of two disappointing defeats, going down 3-1 to Shakhtar Donetsk on October 14 and then 5-1 to Manchester City on October 20.

Marko Nikolic's side have been beaten in four of their last five matches in all competitions, including their last two domestic fixtures against PAOK and Panathinaikos.

The Yellow-Blacks, who are currently 29th in the Champions League table on three points, have faced Real Madrid on four previous occasions and have only lost once.

The first two meetings between these two teams occurred in the UEFA Cup back in 1985, with AEK Athens recording a 1-0 victory in the first leg of their first-round fixture, before Real Madrid posted a 5-0 win in the second leg to comfortably advance.

The duo also locked horns twice in the group stage of the 2002-03 Champions League, and both of those fixtures finished level, including a 3-3 draw in Athens, with the Yellow-Blacks actually unbeaten at home to European heavyweights Real Madrid.

Real Madrid have only been victorious in one of their last eight away UEFA matches against Greek opposition, drawing five times in the process.

Jose Mourinho's side will enter this match in excellent form, though, having won each of their last six matches in all competitions, with the capital giants responding impressively to their 2-1 loss to Atletico Madrid in the Madrid derby before the last international break.

Los Blancos will enter this match off the back of a 3-0 success over Racing de Santander in La Liga, while they beat RB Leipzig 4-1 in their last Champions League fixture.

Real Madrid have a 100% record in this season's Champions League league stage, picking up nine points from three matches, which has left them in fourth spot in the division.

Mourinho's team will take on PSV Eindhoven, Arsenal, LASK Linz and Shakhtar Donetsk in their final four matches in this season's league stage.

AEK Athens will be without the services of Thomas Strakosha (hand), while Joao Mario (illness) and Lazaros Rota (illness) both need to be assessed ahead of the contest.

Former Real Madrid striker Luka Jovic is set to operate through the middle for the hosts; the 28-year-old has been in strong form this season, scoring seven times in 15 appearances.

There is also expected to be a spot through the middle for Barnabas Varga, who is the Greek outfit's leading goalscorer this season with nine in 13 appearances in all competitions.

As for Real Madrid, Vinicius Junior is available, and it is expected that the Brazilian, who is currently serving a domestic ban, will be introduced into the XI down the left.

Federico Valverde is back in training, having recovered from a hamstring issue, and there is a strong chance that the Uruguay international could be in the squad for this fixture.

However, Rodrygo (knee) and Raul Asencio (leg) are definitely out of the clash.

Yan Diomande could start down the right, with Arda Guler dropping back into central midfield, while Jude Bellingham and Kylian Mbappe will feature in the final third of the field.

Brignoli; Rota, Moukoudi, Relvas, Pilo; Majer, Arriaga, Marin, Mario; Jovic, Varga

Courtois; Dumfries, Rudiger, Huijsen, Carreras; Tchouameni, Guler; Diomande, Bellingham, Vinicius; Mbappe

Real Madrid are flying at the moment, and we are fully expecting Los Blancos to secure all three points against an AEK Athens team currently struggling for form.

#1807. Martín Zubimendi open to January Arsenal exit

Martín Zubimendi is open to leaving Arsenal in January in search of regular playing time, according to Graeme Bailey of TEAMtalk. Arsenal is aware of the midfielder’s position and could consider a loan when the window reopens.

Zubimendi played in all 38 Premier League games as Arsenal won the title last season, starting 34 and scoring five goals. Nine games into its title defense, Arsenal has yet to give him a league start.

His role had already begun to change in the spring, when Mikel Arteta gave Myles Lewis-Skelly more time in midfield. Zubimendi was left out of the starting lineup for the Champions League final against Paris Saint-Germain. Competition increased again in August when Bruno Guimarães arrived from Newcastle United.

Arsenal paid close to £60 million to sign Zubimendi in July 2025. He had spent six seasons in Real Sociedad’s first team, making 236 appearances and winning the Copa del Rey alongside Mikel Merino, who later became his teammate again in London.

Zubimendi had been selective about leaving San Sebastián. He turned down Liverpool a year before joining Arsenal and later explained that he still had things he wanted to learn at Sociedad. The chance to work with Arteta helped persuade him to move the following summer.

A return to Spain is one possibility this winter. Real Madrid’s interest emerged in August, when José Mourinho was looking for an experienced midfielder to play in front of his defense. Bailey also names Barcelona and Atlético Madrid as admirers.

Barcelona keeps watch on Lucas Herrington

#1806. 'I'm living my dream and loving every minute': West Brom star HARRY WHITWELL on his first-team breakthrough, James Morrison's words of advice, learning Norwegian and the Baggies' promotion hopes

Published: 22:00 EDT, 29 October 2026 | Updated: 22:00 EDT, 29 October 2026

As Harry Whitwell wheeled away after scoring against Burnley back in August, the home fans in the Hawthorns erupted in unison.

This was more than West Brom supporters celebrating a crucial goal against a potential promotion rival, though. Nine years after joining the Baggies' academy, the 20-year-old Whitwell, the latest academy gem from the club's underrated production line, had delivered a moment that showed he belonged.

‘I didn't really know what to do,’ Whitwell admits to Daily Mail Sport. ‘Growing up in the academy, you're always picturing scoring your first goal in the garden and thinking about what you’d do.

‘That went out the window. I was just taken aback for a little bit, but given I've been at the club for half of my life, it made it extra special.’

Whitwell joined West Brom aged 11 and has enjoyed a breakthrough few months after impressing in pre-season and earning the trust of boss James Morrison.

His goal against Burnley was his first in the league for the club, following an EFL Cup strike against Rotherham a few weeks earlier.

Although usually a central player, he has largely operated on the right of Morrison’s fluid 4-4-2 set-up, making 12 appearances in all competitions as West Brom sit fifth in the Championship. A new contract last month was recognition of his progress.

West Brom youngster Harry Whitwell has enjoyed a breakthrough few months at the club

With Whitwell and Co impressing, the Baggies have moved up to fifth in the Championship

‘It’s what I’ve always wanted, and I’ve loved every minute of it,’ Whitwell says. ‘It took a bit of time from my first game in the FA Cup to break through properly, but to be given a chance at the club you've grown up at is a dream come true.’

Patience has been key. Whitwell made his first-team debut against non-League Aldershot in the FA Cup in January 2024, before his Championship bow came in May 2025. A superb loan spell at Forest Green Rovers followed, but opportunities were limited after he was recalled in January.

He featured just twice in the league during a chaotic campaign in which West Brom narrowly avoided relegation. Morrison answered an SOS call in late February to take charge for a third spell as interim boss, guiding the Baggies to safety with 18 points from 12 games.

Whitwell had no guarantees when he reported for pre-season and was prepared to head out on loan again, but his immediate priority was to impress the coaching staff and see where it led.

Although he barely featured after his recall, he views that period as an invaluable learning experience.

Morrison’s impact over that time saw his role become permanent, and the momentum was carried into a summer rebuild that brought ten new arrivals.

The recruitment focused heavily on young talent at the behest of chairman Shilen Patel, technical director Dominic Price and head of football operations Ian Pearce, with Jimmy-Jay Morgan, Rabby Nzingoula and Toby Collyer among the additions. Norwegian midfielder Felix Horn Myhre, 27, was the only outfield signing older than 23.

Meanwhile, experienced high-earning stars including Karlan Grant, Alex Mowatt, Jed Wallace and Josh Maja departed as the Baggies trimmed their wage bill.

Whitwell is loving working under boss James Morrison (pictured), who has played a big role in his development

He is one of a number of talented youngsters in the Baggies squad, alongside the likes of Jimmy-Jay Morgan (right)

‘It's really exciting,’ Whitwell says. ‘We could be doing better, but to be in the play-off spots is really good. The squad is quite young, but it’s made up of players who are trying to prove themselves and are full of energy.

‘We're maybe just missing that final bit in front of goal to show that we're a team who can really be among it this season at the top.’

Morrison, an Albion legend who made 341 appearances for the club between 2007 and 2019, has played a significant role in Whitwell’s development. He previously coached the midfielder in the academy and handed him his Championship debut against Luton in May 2025.

‘We have a really good relationship,’ Whitwell says. ‘He's provided me with a lot of chances in the first team. With the career he's had, and as a fellow midfielder, I just want to learn as much as I can from him. He's always given little pieces of information which have been helpful and made me see the game a bit differently.

‘Maybe that’s why it’s been a bit more comfortable for me making that jump to the first team too, because I’ve worked with him before and know how he works and what he demands.’

West Brom remain a work in progress, with defeats against rivals Wolves and Birmingham exposing their deficiencies, while they’ve conceded first in their past six games. But there are encouraging signs of quality and resilience, evidenced by comeback wins over Blackburn and Wrexham in recent weeks.

Whitwell is enjoying the atmosphere around the squad and has struck up particularly close friendships with striker Barney Stewart and young goalkeeper Joe Wallis.

Whitwell pictured making his Albion debut in an FA Cup tie against Aldershot in January 2024

The midfielder (right) has made 12 appearances this season and recently signed a new deal

He sits alongside Albion’s Norwegian duo Aune Heggebo and Felix Horn Myhre on the team bus, and even started learning Norwegian on language app Duolingo as a result. That proved to be a struggle, however, with his lessons lasting only a week. Whitwell can at least safely order a coffee and say thank you next time he visits Oslo.

His progress is testament to West Brom’s academy, an often-underappreciated production line that has developed a host of talented stars over the years.

Morgan Rogers left for Man City aged 17 in a £5million move, while the sales of Tom Fellows, Alex Palmer and Dara O’Shea in recent times helped ease the club’s financial pressures under the troubled ownership of Chinese businessman Guochuan Lai, who sold up to Patel in 2024.

Under its manager Richard Stevens, who has just passed seven years at the club, the academy has continued to emphasise that hard work is key to player development. Whitwell, speaking to Daily Mail Sport as part of the EFL’s 'Raised in the EFL' initiative, which celebrates the work of youth systems, is the latest graduate to make the step up.

‘There's a lot of really good people and coaches who are very experienced and good at developing players,’ he says. 'We're hard-working and down to earth, too. The academy doesn't get the money that maybe the big clubs get, but all of our teams are focused on hard work, resilience and technical quality.’

Whitwell looked up to the likes of Fellows, Caleb Taylor and Sam Field during his own academy days and now, having established himself in the first team, he is a key part of a West Brom side that face a significant week before the international break.

A trip to West Ham is followed by back-to-back home games against Southampton and Millwall, and with eighth place now enough to qualify for the play-offs, the Baggies have an opportunity to underline their promotion credentials.

Whitwell sits next to Albion's Norwegian duo Aune Heggebo (right) and Felix Horn Myhre on the team coach and tried to learn their language on Duolingo

The 20-year-old is determined to continue developing and not take anything for granted

For Whitwell, the challenges keep coming but his determination won't waver after committing his future to the club until at least 2029.

‘To get that show of faith and be able to commit the next few years here was a really good feeling but this is just the start,’ he says.

‘I’m not taking anything for granted and just trying to make as many appearances as possible. Hopefully I can get more goals and assists because that's what you get judged on as an attacking player.

‘If we can get a bit of positive momentum leading into the international break, that will put us in a good position. Our home games are massive for us, so we’ve got to make the Hawthorns a fortress.’

#1805. Andoni Iraola: Liverpool cannot ‘sustain the level’ I want

Andoni Iraola has conceded that Liverpool cannot currently “sustain the level” he expects after his side squandered a two-goal lead for the second match in a row.

In the Spaniard’s first game at Anfield since becoming manager, Monaco fought back to win 3-2 by virtue of Paris Brunner’s late glancing header seven days on from Leeds United’s 4-2 victory in Chicago, emphasising Liverpool’s alarming lack of depth, particularly in defence.

“We played a good first half, especially a good 30 minutes. Right now we probably don’t have much more, in terms of the levels required to play like this. They deserved to turn around the game.

“We won the first two pre-season games, but the last two we cannot sustain the level we want for all of the game. As soon as we made some changes, players start to get tired and we cannot sustain that level. So, we have work to do.”

Alex on target 🎯 pic.twitter.com/PT6AYrLxyz

Alisson, Virgil van Dijk and Cody Gakpo all made their first appearances and contributed to a lively first-half in which Iraola’s commitment to man-to-man marking and an intensive pressing structure were evident out of possession. With the ball in the first half they demonstrated the kind of slick passing that Bournemouth employed to carve opponents open on the counter-attack.

A nimble one-two between Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai allowed the Dutch midfielder to set up Alexander Isak to score with a shot from 16 yards and the most expensive player in English football history laid claim to the second, too, when he seemed to hook in a rebound from Lukas Hradecky’s save while lying in the six-yard box.

Later he would graciously acknowledge that he and Florian Wirtz had connected with the ball simultaneously and he was happy to yield the credit to his team-mate.

Our second goal of the game, scored by Wirtz… we think 🤔 pic.twitter.com/FUzA363Oxw

At that point it seemed that victory would be a cakewalk but just before half-time Aleksandr Golovin caught Van Dijk out with a feint and late swerve to the right, tripping over the Liverpool captain’s clumsy hack. Despite a heavy limp, Golovin hammered the penalty past Alisson’s dive to make it 2-1 at the break.

Iraola rationed his early changes at the start of the second half to two but Liverpool could not regain their rhythm and Mika Biereth capitalised on a Gravenberch error to score the equaliser after battling to be first to the rebound when Giorgi Mamardashvili saved his first effort, stroking his effort through Wataru Endo’s legs.

Cue five substitutions as soon as that goal had gone in and a raft more followed, killing the remaining half-hour of all momentum and cohesion. By the time Brunner exploited a dozy mix-up between Milos Kerkez and Federico Chiesa about whose responsibility he was at a corner to flash his header past Mamardashvili, only two of the 22 starters were still on the pitch.

Liverpool: Alisson (Mamardashvili 46), Tsimikas (Kerkez 59), Van Dijk (c) (Chambers 59), Ndukwe (Endo 46), Frimpong (Ramsay 75), Gravenberch (Nyoni 59), Gakpo (Ngumoha 59), Wirtz (McConnell 59), Koumas (Chiesa 75), Isak (Muñoz 59)Substitutes: Morrison, Davies.Goals: Isak (16), Wirtz (29)Monaco: Hradecky, Nazinho (Mawissa 75), Dier (c) (Kehrer 75), S Sané, Vanderson (Teze 46), Golovin (Idumbo 75), Cabral (Soubeir 75), Camara (Benzahra 64), Detourbet (Coulibaly 64), Biereth (Brunner 80), Abline (Konaté 64).Substitutes: Assab, Kohn, Lienard, Nibombe, Touré.  Goals: Golovin (44 pen), Biereth (56), Brunner (88)

They played well in the first half, as they did against Leeds, but lost all shape and structure in the second half to lose 3-2.

Yellow card for Konate for clattering into Endo late. That’s the last of the action.

Liverpool 2 Monaco 3 (Brunner)  Brilliant near-post glancing header from a devilishly whippy, dipping corner. Kerkez doing his best Rip van Winkle impression.

Diligent defensive work by Ngumoha stops Konate’s run down the outside left.

A final substitution, hopefully. Brunner replaces Biereth. Konate’s shot, a pearoller, is easily saved by Mamardashvili after A mix-up between Kerkez and Munoz.

As usual, the substitutions have killed the game. Watched Leeds vs RB Leipzig yesterday. They played two 60 minute matches which kept it more competitive for longer but still descended into a kickabout late on.

Mawissa, Kehrer, Idumbo and Soubeir have replaced Nazinho, Dier, Golovin and Cabral.

Monaco also made changes, four I think. Will catch up with then once they’re confirmed. Ramsey is into the game straight away tp stop Coulibaly’s shot.

Ramsay, Chiesa and Elliott are coming on for Szoboszlai, Frimpong and Koumas. Lovely applause for Elliott.

Konate sweeps a left-foot shot from the left of the box past the right post with Mamardashvili forced into a headlong dive. Liverpool have lost their defensive shape and intensity, allowing Monaco to punch holes through the lines with some direct running.

Nazinho gets round Frimpong down the Monaco left and cuts back the perfect pass to put it on a plate for Coulibaly who hammers a left-foot shot from the right of the D that Mamardashvili throws up his hands to block. That would have stung. Good save. A flag would have meant it wouldn’t have counted but even so Frimpong’s defensive work wasn’t good enough.

It’s been very scrappy since the changes but then Ngumoha pounces on to a loose ball, glides up the right and tries to play Koumas in behind the back four. Sadly, he overhits the pass which trickles out for a goal-kick. Cue an ovation and cries of ‘Rio! Rio!’

Three changes for Monaco with Detoubet, Abline and Camara departing for Benzhara, Coulibaly and Konaté.

Ngumoha has gone to the right wing and Koumas is playing through the middle as a false nine.

Liverpool make five changes with Gakpo, Van Dijk, Wirtz, Tsimikas and Isak departing while Munoz makes his ‘debut’ with Ngumoha, Nyoni, Chambers, McConell and Kerkez.

Liverpool 2 Monaco 2 (Biereth) Mistake by Gravenberch allows Golovin to play a pass into the left half of the box for Biereth. His first shot is well saved by Mamardashvili at full stretch but his tenacity allowed him to get to the rebound ahead of Endo, swivel and stick his second effort in to equalise.

Monaco overplay at the edge of the box, Detourbet, Biereth and Abline playing ‘after you. Claud’, instead of shooting.

A slick, short passing move between Gravenberch, Wirtz and Isak ends with Isak on the deck in the box after Gravenberch’s step-over allowed the ball to run to him. Isak took a touch to move the ball on to his left but gave the defender a glimmer of it and he hacked it away before felling Isak as well as collateral damage.

Quiet start to the half. Biereth just pressed Mamardashvili but the keeper managed to sweep the ball away even though under more pressure than he would have expected.

Liverpool try to play out from the back with Mamardashvili spearing a straight pass to Gravenberch who tried to knock it round the corner for Endo but the ball skidded under his studs and out for a throw-in.

Isak is apparently claiming both goals. Replays are indistinct. He could have clipped it in off his heel as he had a swing at the ball while grounded at the same time as Wirtz.

Our second goal of the game, scored by Wirtz… we think 🤔 pic.twitter.com/FUzA363Oxw

Endo has slotted in at centre-back alongside Van Dijk.

Half-time changes: Mamardashvili for Alisson and Endo for Ndukwe.

For Monaco, Teze for Vanderson at right-back.

Much to admire in that first-half performance from Liverpool’s front six and centre-backs, the latter two particularly out of possession and winning it back. The man-to-man system is working well for them. But they should be out of sight by now instead of leading by only a goal.

Liverpool free-kick on the right after a foul on Koumas. Szoboszlai whips in the cross and Van Dijk gets up first to the left of the penalty spot but bludgeons his header about a foot wide of the right post.

Charlie Adam says the penalty was ‘a soft one’ but Van Dijk did not adjust when Golovin shifted it to his right, stuck out a leg and Golovim understandably decided to topple over the hurdle.

Liverpool 2 Monaco 1 (Golovin, pen) Speared it into the top right. Alisson went the right way but was beaten for pace and power.

The referee, Jarred Gillett, gives Monaco a penalty. It was deserved, too. Golovin went on a driving run down the middle, shifted it to his right and was tripped by Van Dijk.

Liverpool are well worth their lead. They are streets ahead of Monaco.

A microcosm of the game so far: Liverpool pass goes astray, a player wins it back – this time Gakpo – by snapping into a tackle before laying it off to his left for the unmarked Tsimikas to skim a low shot about a foot wide of the left post from 25 yards.

Monaco have done very little since that wee salvo in the opening minute but just now Abline was given too much space from distance but whacked his shot into the Kop.

Big cheer from the crowd for Hugo Ekitike

The impressive Koumas diddles Nazinho with a Cruyff turn but then thumps his shot straight into Hradecky’s chest.

Liverpool 2 Monaco 0 (Wirtz) Pass chipped out to Koumas down the right who arcs a cross to the back post. Gakpo meets it with a header back across goal to Isak whose first effort from a couple of yards is blocked but the ball gets stuck under Isak’s falling body and Wirtz is Johnny on the Spot to stab it in from a 18 inches as Dier tried to scramble it away.

Liverpool have been impressive so far but if there has been a weakness it’s still the balance in central midfield defensively. Going forward both Gravenberch and Szobiszlai have dovetailed together well. They win the ball back when Van Dijk steps out and the midfield two fly forward to tee up Koumas for a shot that strikes Dier.

Chance for Wirtz, who opens his body from the left of the D to try to bend a shot into the bottom right corner but fizzes it the wrong side of the post.

It’s been pretty breathless since the goal, Liverpool dozily letting Monaco through the middle before twice cutting Monaco apart in midfield only for Isak to overrun a pass in the box delivered by Wirtz and then Koumas to shoot over.

Liverpool 1 Monaco 0 (Isak) Chip to Gakpo down the left of the box, he clips it first time back to Gravenberch in the D who lays it off to Szoboszlai. Ping-ping-ping. Szoboszlai keeps the tempo high with return, the one in the one-two with Gravenberch who picks out Isak to bury a shot from about 15 yards into the bottom left corner.

Alex on target 🎯 pic.twitter.com/PT6AYrLxyz

Excellent move from Liverpool, instigated by Ndukwe’s fine tackle on Biereth. He knocks it short to Gravenberch who arrows a 60-yard pass out to Koumas hurtling down the right. He measures his cross perfectly for Gakpo stealing in off the left wing and though he connects powerfully with the meat of his brow, he bashes it straight at the keeper. He was offside in any case, it transpires.

Charlie Adam on co-comms points out that Liverpool are going man-to-man now in classic Iraola/Bielsa style and when the camera goes high you can see it, especially with the full-backs.

Liverpool are carving the middle of the park up with incisive passing. Szoboszlai starts a move that sends Isak down the left of the box. He traps the chip, turns back to face away from goal and taps a pass back to Wirtz who gallops on to it and bends a shot that Hradecky dives low to his left to beat away with a firm left wrist. Frimpong pounces on the rebound and clips a tame effort straight at Hradecky who had quickly restored himself to the vertical.

Van Dijk gobbles up a long pass over Ndukwe, snuffing out any possibility of Biereth getting there first.

Tsimikas is free down the left but overhits his cross on the run when Isak was begging for a cut-back. The left-back went for the back post and ballooned his centre behind, miles beyond Koumas and Wirtz.

Liverpool defend the corner solidly and Frimpong races away on the counter, bombing on to the ball and sprinting into the Monaco half. But his touch is not as sound as his pace and Monaco deal with him when he fluffs his control.

A period of applause in memory of Kevin Keegan ❤️ pic.twitter.com/AkPZG7babe

Liverpool kick off defending the Kop. They roll the ball back to Frimpong who chips a long pass up the right to Koumas who hares on to the pass down the right and crosses, just beyond Isak. Hradecky gathers and bowls the ball out. A mistake by Tisimikas lets Biereth barrel through the inside-right to hammer a shot that Alisson turns behind for a corner.

The crowd applauds in the modern way. My goodness he was a terrific player. Saw him play for Liverpool, Southampton and Newcastle. Absolutely relentless.

Virgil van Dijk has the pennant. Liverpool are wearing all red with the paint splashes of the 1990 kit. Monaco are in a very pale green.

For me it’s a special game, most of the players and people will be ‘it’s [just] a pre-season friendly’, but for me it’s a lot more than this. It will be the first time I have the chance to go out, to feel this stadium and I hope we can also perform well.

It’s a good game for us, because it’s going to be demanding, it’s a team that wants to dominate and they also want to press high so we will see how we are.

I think the cases of Ali[sson], Cody, and Virgil I think it’s their first game. It shouldn’t go longer than 45 minutes, maybe a little bit more if they feel comfortable.

Also for some of the others Ryan, Flo, and Alex, it’s the second game so we have to be aware of those things.

But the league starts in two weeks, so we cannot wait also too much; we have to give them quality minutes.

I think today is going to be a good reference, two games – Monaco and Como – teams that try dominate the game, they are very good in possession, so they will demand us the best without the ball. If we want to control the game and also physical teams, they are probably a very good test.

I hope we are at the level and we can do very good games.

Liverpool Alisson; Frimpong, Ndukwe, Van Dijk, Tsimikas; Szoboszlai, Gakpo; Koumaz, Wirtz, Gakpo; Isak.

Monaco Hradecky; Vanderson, Dier, Sané, Nazinho; Detourbet, Cabral, Camara, Golovin, Abline, Biereth.

Le 𝐗𝐈 qui débutera cette rencontre face à 𝐋𝐢𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐩𝐨𝐨𝐥 📋 pic.twitter.com/2cOYRbzUEN

🥳 Feliz aniversário, 𝐅𝐢𝐥𝐢𝐩𝐞 𝐋𝐮𝐢́𝐬! 🎉Notre coach fête aujourd'hui ses 41 ans 🎂 pic.twitter.com/VTd4BQ5rRK

Alisson, Van Dijk and Gakpo return, Ndukwe continues in defence.

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of the first of two Liverpool home friendlies after their preseason tour of the United States. Andoni Iraola’s side saw off Wrexham and Sunderland in their first two matches but gave away a two-goal lead at half-time in the final fixture and ended up being beaten 4-2 by Leeds United in Chicago in the last game after multiple changes. What did we learn? Not a huge amount in the absence of Virgil van Dijk, Alisson, Víctor Muñoz, Cody Gakpo and Alexis Mac Allister, the first four of whom are available today other than an ongoing vulnerability from set-pieces and Curtis Jones looking like he is in desperate need of a fresh start.

This afternoon at Anfield they take on AS Monaco who finished seventh in Ligue 1 this season but are under new management with the recruitment of the former Chelsea and Atlético left-back Filipe Luís as head coach. It’s quite the coup for Le Rocher given he led Flamengo to their first Brazilian title in five years, the Copa Libertadores and the Copa do Brasil in his 18 months in charge.

In pre-season so far he has overseen a 5-2 win over fourth-tier AS Saint-Priest, a 2-0 defeat by Sporting Clube, a 2-2 draw with Cercle Bruges and a 1-0 victory over Getafe. They have sold their best player, Maghnes Akliouche, to PSG for £43m and Aladji Bamba to Newcastle for £34m but have so far retained Mamadou Coulibaly and Folarin Balogun, signed and made Ansu Fati’s loan move into a long-term deal.

Iraola may well persevere with Trey Nyoni in midfield who, after his performances on tour, ought to be on the threshold of a breakthrough season and it would be interesting to see him paired with Ryan Gravenberch just behind Dominik Szoboszlai.

Ifeanyi Ndukwe, who played well in America after coming on for the injured Joe Gomez, does not have a UK work permit and will have to go abroad on loan for the season but Jérémy Jacquet, who has yet to feature, was due to have a fitness test this morning and would be a welcome to boost to a squad whose defence still requires significant reinforcements.

#1804. Allegri: Napoli’s Champions League fate in our own hands

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Despite growing pressure amid inconsistent results, Massimiliano Allegri is confident Napoli's Champions League fate is in their own hands.

Napoli lost their opening two matches of their European campaign – going down to Arsenal and Villarreal – though they prevailed in a seven-goal thriller against Bodo/Glimt last time out.

Heading into the halfway point of the league phase, Napoli currently sit 22nd in the table, inside the play-off places on goal difference.

Napoli are now looking for back-to-back Champions League wins for the first time since March 2023 (two, both v Eintracht Frankfurt).

But Allegri is not yet worried about their European form, insisting that their destiny will still be in their own control no matter the result against Porto on Wednesday.

"There are some small details missing that allow us to get results," Allegri told Sky Sport Italia when asked what was missing from his side's performances.

"This inconsistent performance we're having in the league is proof of that. In the Champions League, we lost the first two and then won at home against Bodo/Glimt.

"But I believe that in the Champions League, regardless of [the Porto] match, our fate will be in our hands against Manchester City, because with 10 points, we can qualify for the play-offs, and that would be a great achievement.

"We need to try to play [on Wednesday], prepare for the match against Lazio, and then spend the break trying to recover as many players as possible to try to rotate them."

Ready to go again #UCL https://t.co/oYlqfYePom

— UEFA Champions League (@ChampionsLeague) November 2, 2026

Napoli were on a three-game unbeaten streak in all competitions, which started with the 4-3 win over Bodo, but that came to a halt against Juventus on Sunday.

They are seeking a much-needed confidence boost, though it could prove difficult; Porto are unbeaten in six when hosting Serie A opposition in European competition, winning four of them (D2).

Porto have won each of their last 10 league games, but they have struggled at home in the Champions League, losing both such matches so far.

"The game is difficult because Porto have won 10 in a row in the league, and they've played some good games in the Champions League too," Allegri added in his press conference.

"As for us, talking is of little use; we need to put in a good performance.

"Right now, it's time to act, not to talk. It's not an easy moment. We've had mixed results and haven't yet managed to win two league games in a row.

"But what's certain is that we have to keep working and try to turn things around in the league. In the meantime, we're thinking about [Wednesday]; there's a game to play."

Napoli could receive a late double injury boost. Rasmus Hojlund has had the flu, while Kevin De Bruyne, who has created 10 chances from open play in the Champions League this season, has an ankle injury.

But Allegri is hopeful they could play some part against Porto.

"Hojlund's fever has gone. De Bruyne will train, and afterwards we'll see if he's available," Allegri said of the duo.

Jack Grealish is expected to be left out of Everton’s squad for tonight’s Premier League clash away against Newcastle United, according to a report.

The 31-year-old was omitted from the senior squad for the Toffees’ EFL Cup home win over the Magpies on Thursday due to a ‘breach of club discipline’.

Although manager David Moyes did not confirmed the exact reason behind Grealish’s absence, it is understood that the winger failed to show up for a training session in the build-up to the fourth-round tie.

The Manchester City loanee had previously missed Everton’s 2-0 Premier League defeat at Arsenal just over a week ago due to illness.

According to The Athletic, Grealish is 'not fit' to face Newcastle and has subsequently not travelled with the rest of Everton’s squad for this evening’s game at St James’ Park.

The report adds that it is unclear whether Grealish will return for Everton’s next fixture at home to Coventry City on Friday.

Speaking after Everton’s EFL Cup win, Moyes revealed that he supported the club’s decision to drop Grealish, but refused to comment further on the matter.

Grealish is in his second season on loan at Everton from Man City; a long-term injury cut his first spell short, but his standout early performances made him a massive hit with the fans.

However, the winger has struggled to make his mark this term, failing to score or assist in any of his eight appearances across all competitions.

#1801. ‘You still haven’t seen the best version of me’ at Liverpool, insists Barcola

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Bradley Barcola insists he has not yet hit his best level at Liverpool, though he is confident that will come as he continues to adapt to the team.

Barcola joined Liverpool from Paris Saint-Germain for a reported £123m in another big-money signing for the Reds this summer.

He has made a slow start to life at Anfield, creating some concern that he could take a while to settle in, following in the footsteps of Alexander Isak – who is beginning to hit his stride this season – and Florian Wirtz, both of whom joined last year.

Barcola has made 12 appearances for Liverpool in all competitions, failing to get a goal involvement in each of his first six.

However, there have been promising signs in recent weeks: following a hat-trick against LASK in the Champions League, Barcola then got assists in back-to-back Premier League games.

The Frenchman is confident that spending more time with his new team-mates will help him to unlock his best level.

"No, I don't think I'm at my best yet," Barcola told Sky Sports. "You still haven't seen the best version of me.

"On top of that, we're working with my team-mates, so that they can make the most of my strengths.

"So yes, I think once we really develop that understanding, things will get much better. And I think things are improving all the time.

"People are beginning to understand my style of play much better. I think it's going much better."

Previously in the 2026/27 #UCL https://t.co/LoH7b3Xt5C

Barcola was also brought to Merseyside in the wake of Mohamed Salah's exit, with some assuming he would act as a replacement for the Egyptian – who left as the club’s all-time Premier League goalscorer (191) and assister (93).

"First of all, I wasn't the one who decided the transfer fee," he added. "So that's not been my problem.

"And regarding Mo Salah, he's a legend here. A huge one. He's done big things here, and for that I have an enormous respect for him. But it's not pressure for me at all.

"I'm not Mohamed Salah, so I'm going to try to contribute whatever I can to the club and make my own mark on its history. I don't feel any pressure about that."

Barcola left PSG after making 152 appearances in all competitions – netting 39 goals in that time – and having enjoyed a trophy-laden spell.

He won three Ligue 1 titles, two Champions Leagues, two Super Cups, and the Coupe de France twice.

"For me, it was the right time to leave PSG," he said. "I spent so many great years there, and I won an enormous amount of trophies. But it was time.

"It was quite difficult because, over there, it was a real family. We'd built something very special together. On top of that, it was very difficult to leave and say goodbye to my team-mates. But ultimately, that's just how football is.

"When a club like Liverpool comes calling, it's a great thing. I didn't have any doubts, and I just knew I had to come here. I'm happy to be here, and I hope things go well for PSG."

#1799. From A-League champions to liquidation sale - inside the auction of Western United's remaining assets

Published: 01:36 EDT, 30 October 2026 | Updated: 01:37 EDT, 30 October 2026

Four years after lifting the A-League trophy and promising a glittering future in Melbourne's west, Western United is selling off the remnants of its football operation to the highest bidder.

The remains of the former champions' operation are heading to auction, with everything from giant television screens and espresso machines to gym equipment and shipping containers up for grabs.

Auction house Manheim has advertised a 96-lot liquidation sale, offering a glimpse of what remains of the club's operation after its ambitious plans for Melbourne's west unravelled.

Bidding is scheduled to open at 10am on December 3 and close at 2pm on December 9, with the goods listed in Altona North, Melbourne.

And there is considerably more on offer than a few spare footballs.

Anyone looking to upgrade their viewing experience can browse 86-inch LG monitors alongside a collection of Philips screens ranging from 50 to 75 inches.

Western United's equipment is heading to auction after the former A-League champions' financial collapse

Even Western United's shipping container ticket booths will go under the hammer

Televisions and whitegoods are among the items being sold from the former A-League club

The laundry equipment includes LG and Samsung washing machines, plus LG and Speed Queen dryers.

There are Smeg ovens and dishwashers, La Pavoni espresso machines and a commercial oven/warmer, giving the sale something of a kitchen showroom feel.

Even the office furniture is going, with desks, chairs, a glass table, printers and an Epson projector and screen among the listings.

For supporters who would prefer to train like a professional footballer, the catalogue includes spin bikes, squat racks, dumbbells, barbells and a leg press. Two recovery baths and a Pilates machine are also listed.

Then there are the shipping containers, with multiple custom units and three described as 20-foot containers included in the sale.

The sale marks a dramatic turnaround for a club that entered the A-League in 2019 promising a privately owned stadium and a permanent foothold in Melbourne's western suburbs.

Western United reached the pinnacle of the men's competition in 2022 under coach John Aloisi.

Four years later, its equipment is being sold on behalf of a liquidator.

Auction house Manheim is handling the sale on behalf of the liquidator

Recovery baths and specialised player-testing equipment offer a glimpse inside the professional football operation

The sale catalogue features 96 lots of sporting equipment and general goods

The club's financial troubles had included a reported $15.5million Australian Taxation Office debt, while a proposed $100million takeover by American group KAM Sports failed to proceed.

Western United sat out the 2025-26 A-League season in hibernation, initially insisting: 'This is not a farewell, nor is it a step back.'

But the hoped-for comeback never arrived.

The Australian Professional Leagues terminated its participation agreement in August, ending its involvement in both the men's and women's A-League competitions.

APL chairperson Stephen Conroy said the club had breached several obligations, including requirements under Football Australia's National Club Licensing Regulations.

The damage extended well beyond the senior professional teams.

Football Victoria announced on August 12 that Western United would be withdrawn from all its competitions after the Federal Court ordered WMG Football Club Limited to be wound up in insolvency.

The entity was the company through which Western United participated in the Victorian competitions.

Football Victoria said it had explored every available option to allow the teams to finish their seasons, but could find no viable pathway following the court decision.

Young players were left unable to register with another club for the final weeks of the season under registration regulations.

'For many of these young players, WUFC has been a significant part of their football journey and we understand how disappointing and unsettling this news will be for them and their families,' FV chief executive Dan Birrell said.

The withdrawal also forced Western United's results to be removed from the relevant senior and junior competitions, triggering ladder recalculations and leaving byes in the remaining fixtures.

#1798. Lens vs Como - prediction, team news, lineups

By Jonathan O'Shea | 02 Nov 2026 15:38, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 14:16

Languishing outside the Champions League's top 24, Lens will aim to move level with Como when they meet at Stade Bollaert-Delelis on Wednesday night.

Following their historic defeat of Manchester United, the Italian debutants have put six points on the board, while their hosts only have three and lie below the playoff zone.

Since Lens started their fourth Champions League campaign with a thrilling 3-2 comeback win over Slavia Prague, the French club have come away empty-handed from their subsequent fixtures.

Les Sang et Or were first beaten 2-0 at home by Sporting Lisbon, then suffered another defeat on their travels, going down 3-0 to Club Brugge.

Remarkably, 16 games and some 28 years have now passed since they last kept a clean sheet in the Champions League.

Lens returned to Europe's top table by finishing second in Ligue 1 last term but, after a slow start, new boss Dino Toppmoller swiftly made way for Yannick Cahuzac.

Though Toppmoller's former assistant started positively with three straight league wins, his side were beaten by their bitter local rivals last time out.

With a late Olivier Giroud goal, Lille snatched victory in the 125th Derby du Nord on Friday night, leaving Lens ninth in the French top flight.

Now, Cahuzac's side must try to respond with maximum points, as they surely need at least two more wins from five remaining Champions League matches.

Como took one step closer to the knockout phase last month, thumping Manchester United 4-1 on a memorable night at Stadio Sinigaglia, where main man Nico Paz bagged a brace.

Regardless of United's dire state, that marked an incredible achievement for a club promoted back to Italy's top tier only two years earlier - and they were down in Serie D as recently as 2019.

Expertly led by Cesc Fabregas, 10 goals from their first three games is the best haul of any debutant in UEFA's elite competition since 1973 - and each one has been scored from open play.

Paz and top scorer Tasos Douvikas already have five Champions League strikes between them, and the pair have been even more productive in Serie A, with 11 goal involvements combined.

Since losing 3-2 to Feyenoord on matchday two, Como have embarked on a streak of five consecutive wins across all competitions, scoring 13 goals and conceding just three.

New France cap Lucas Da Cunha was decisive from the spot in Sunday's 1-0 victory against rock-bottom Venezia, taking the Lariani up to a club-record tally of 23 points from their opening 10 games.

Now occupying fourth place - where they finished last term - Como are closely in touch with Italy's current top three, and few would rule them out of the Scudetto race.

Lens will be missing several men on Wednesday, with defensive duo Ismaelo Ganiou and Maik Nawrocki joining forwards Abdalllah Sima and Odsonne Edouard on the sidelines.

The latter has undergone surgery for an adductor injury and could be ruled out until 2027, so Franjo Ivanovic is expected to lead the home side's attack.

Still struggling with a hamstring problem, Ecuadorian wing-back Jhoanner Chavez is also a doubt.

While veteran playmaker Florian Thauvin has created the most chances across the Champions League's opening three matchdays (15), Como star Paz has been directly involved in five goals.

Douvikas has scored in all three of the Lariani's league-phase appearances, so they are both integral parts of the Fabregas plan.

The Catalan coach will still be without Moise Kean, Trevoh Chalobah, Jesus Rodriguez and Assane Diao due to injury, while Jayden Addai is a major doubt.

Sometimes rotated with Chelsea loanee Robert Sanchez, goalkeeper Jean Butez recently replaced Robin Risser of Lens in the France squad.

Risser; Aguilar, Baidoo, Todibo; Abdulhamid, Cuisance, Haidara, Udol; Thauvin, Sotoca; Ivanovic

Butez; Smolcic, Kempf, Ramon, Valle; Perrone, Ricci; Da Cunha, Paz, Baturina; Douvikas

Although the sample size is small, Como tend to start sharply in Europe, having scored first - and during the first half - in all three of their Champions League matches.

The Lariani also possess a potency that Lens simply cannot withstand, so they will move up to nine points and leave their hosts stranded on three.

#1796. Unbeaten run, a rare free-kick and more: All the key stats from AC Milan 3-1 Inter

As is often the case with the derby win, there were a lot of fun facts and stats to delve into after the full-time whistle, including a free-kick rarity from Diego Moreira.

Many headed into the Derby della Madonnina with a lot of worry considering Inter’s strong start to the season, as well as Milan’s mid-week defeat to Bologna. However, it turned out to be a great evening for the Rossoneri, who clinched all three points in a 3-1 win.

Diego Moreira played a key role in the success, bagging one goal and two assists, while Ruben Amorim got his tactics right as well. In short, it was just what they needed and as is often the case after a huge win, a lot of fun stats emerged afterwards.

Starting with the general stats, it’s clear that Milan made the most of their chances with a 0.66 xG and three goals scored. Moreira’s free-kick obviously didn’t yield a high xG, nor did Adrien Rabiot’s tidy effort, and Christian Pulisic’s header wasn’t super easy to pull off.

Inter had some good chances from close range, parried by Mike Maignan, so that is probably why their xG is higher. Alessandro Bastoni’s header was also an easy one, unlike Pulisic’s, but it was nice to see Milan be the efficient team for once.

The possession is linked to the above, really, as Milan sat back a lot after scoring their goals. Tactically, they played it to perfection and Inter didn’t really create much with all that possession in the end.

This deserves a section of its own because Milan’s recent record in the derby is truly amazing. After losing six games on the trot, the Rossoneri have certainly turned things around with six wins in the last eight encounters and no defeats!

Now the Inter fans can feel some of the pain that we experienced a while back… It’s not just that the Nerazzurri as a club have been really poor against Milan, it’s also that Cristian Chivu has failed completely.

Winning trophies is the most important thing, he’s absolutely right, but there is no question that the derby record is bothering him. As reported by Opta, he’s only the third manager to lose his first three derbies after Leonardo (2009-2011) and Massimo Giacomini (1979-1980).

Like we said at the start, a lot of fun facts emerged from the win last night and giving each of them a section would be a little silly. From a rare free-kick goal in the derby to a midfielder in red-hot form, we have listed them below.

Moreira’s free-kick: Since Opta started collecting the stats in 2004-05, Milan have only scored three direct free-kick goals against Inter in all competitions, with Moreira’s being the latest one. Pirlo (2007) and Theo Hernandez (2025) were the first two.

Pulisic’s speedy start: Pulisic’s goal is the fastest Milan have scored in a league derby against Inter since the 2010-11 season, when Alexandre Pato found the back of the net after a mere 43 seconds. Talk about getting off the right foot.

Rabiot’s goal contributions: Rabiot has become the third Milan midfielder to have at least one goal contribution in five consecutive league games since 2004-05, following in the footsteps of Hakan Calhanoglu (in 2020) and Ricky Kaka (2004 and 2008).
