#1689. Arsenal play like the champions they are as title defence starts with a bang

Mentally liberated and physically rested, Arsenal began the new Premier League campaign with a performance befitting champions. Gone are the anxieties of last season, when the title race gnawed away at their minds and bodies. Gone are the pressures of chasing a first Premier League trophy in more than two decades. Arsenal look slick, refreshed and hungry for more.

“Champions of England, we know what we are,” sang the home supporters in this thrashing of promoted Coventry City. The players moved with the same energy and confidence, as they dominated every aspect of this match against Frank Lampard’s side.

There will, of course, be many tougher games than this one over the course of the season. But there can be no doubt that Arsenal are settled and strong. Everywhere Coventry looked, they saw world-class opponents who knew exactly what to do and where to be. This was Coventry’s first Premier League match since 2001 and it was a reminder, as if one was needed, of the size of the gulf between England’s top two divisions. Thankfully for Lampard, his season will not be decided by matches against teams of Arsenal’s quality.

As it was in last weekend’s Community Shield victory over Manchester City, Mikel Arteta’s side purred and flowed in attack. The rejuvenated Martin Odegaard scored again, as did his close friend Kai Havertz. Bukayo Saka also struck, easing any lingering concerns about his fitness. Both Saka and Declan Rice, who endured such draining campaigns last year, looked sharp.

"The champions are on their way!" Kai Havertz sweeps home from the edge of the box to give Arsenal an early lead against Coventry 👏 pic.twitter.com/SNtrMSPkYJ

There was also another promising performance by new signing Christos Tzolis, while midfield dynamo Myles Lewis-Skelly continued where he left off at the end of last season: winning tackles, spinning past opponents and firing up the home crowd. New face Bruno Guimarães, absent through injury for a few days, was certainly not needed here.

“They know how to do it,” Arteta said of his players. “They know what they have to do. There was a lot to like in the performance. The manner we started the game, with such domination, clarity, understanding and flow, it was really impressive. At this level the players have to be decisive. They were certainly decisive today.”

Coventry had attempted to irritate Arsenal with physicality and direct passes, but it never looked likely to work, despite the best efforts of strikers Ellis Sims and Taiwo Awoniyi. They will not be the first team to struggle against Arsenal’s defenders, and this will not be the first occasion in which their goalkeeper Carl Rushworth is kept busy.

“Arsenal were the best team in the league last year and they showed it,” Lampard said. “They played like it. The noise here at the start of the game, it was different. I remember that noise. It’s different to the Championship.”

"They played like champions" 🏆Frank Lampard said Coventry will learn lessons after their 3-0 opening day defeat to Arsenal ❌ pic.twitter.com/wqA2kngUVt

Before this opening match, Arteta had objected to the idea that Arsenal were planning to “defend” their title. Instead, he said, they are going to “attack” the Premier League once again. It was a classic Arteta-ism, but the manager’s meaning was clear: he wants his team to be aggressive, inventive and courageous. Perhaps more so than in the second half of last season, when their defending was a greater strength than their attacking.

If that was a case of Arteta talking the talk, then his players happily followed it up by walking the walk here. Arsenal played with an unmistakable swagger, as if they simply knew there would only be one outcome against a group of Coventry players with limited experience at this level.

The energy of the home supporters, as buoyant as you might expect following last season’s triumph, undoubtedly helped Arsenal. There were none of the nerves that defined the run-in in the spring, with the fans instead in a partying mood from the moment new signing Ezri Konsa was introduced to the Emirates Stadium before kick-off.

The opening goal took only 15 minutes to arrive, as Havertz swept in an accurate finish from Riccardo Calafiori’s low cross. It has been a good summer for Havertz, who missed so much of last season with injury but has found some rhythm over the past few months. Including friendlies and his performances for Germany at the World Cup, this was his 10th goal in his last 17 appearances.

Coventry have invested in some powerful, commanding players this summer, but there were signs that the physical battle was proving difficult for Lampard’s side. Caleb Yirenkyi is their new club-record signing in midfield, but he was brutally thrown to the floor by Lewis-Skelly in the first half.

Saka’s goal was the result of a quick cross by Tzolis, the new £34m winger who has made such an exciting start to his Arsenal career. The Greek forward was the star of the first half, constantly making things happen, and his delivery was diverted into Saka’s path after 23 minutes.

"Saka couldn't miss!"Arsenal are cruising against Coventry as Bukayo Saka fires home from close range 💥 pic.twitter.com/er411Bi1wh

Odegaard showed in the Community Shield that he is in a more confident place than the last campaign, when he constantly battled injuries, and his early-season form continued here. His goal was scruffy, bobbled in off the right foot, but his all-round performance was typically smooth. With two goals in two games, he has already beaten his tally from last season.

"It's a top finish I would say" 😂Martin Odegaard reacts to his goal against Coventry! pic.twitter.com/mciFfZ6Fhx

From there, the game was over. Arsenal could remove Saka, Rice and Odegaard, safe in the knowledge that their work was done. A comfortable night for the champions, and the perfect start.

"How are you going to keep everyone happy? Winning." 🔥Mikel Arteta reveals his secret for keeping his full squad content after Arsenal's 3-0 win against Coventry 👀 pic.twitter.com/IarLijhd6I

"I think we can do even better to be fair" Martin Odegaard reflects on Arsenal's win over Coventry in the first game of the season 💭 pic.twitter.com/nB2YW83VlE

It’s all over in the capital and Arsenal have started their reign as Premier League champions with a confident and assured three-goal victory over newly-promoted Coventry. Havertz, Saka and Odegaard were all on target in a flawless team performance from Arteta’s men. It’s been a tough evening for Lampard’s side, who simply couldn’t handle Arsenal.

FULL-TIME: Arsenal cruise to victory against Coventry on the opening day of the new season! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/ctybTEor9J

There will be four minutes of added time to round this game off. Merino shoots from long range and aims for the bottom corner, but Rushworth dives to his left and makes the stop.

Awoniyi tries to make a run in behind Arsenal’s defence and latch onto Hamer’s pass. The striker is hauled to the ground by Mosquera, who is lucky to escape a booking. The resulting delivery is smacked straight out of play by Torp. That is such a disappointing cross.

Torp swings a cross into Rudoni, who makes a run from deep. Rudoni meets the delivery, but his glancing header is straight at Raya. It’s Coventry’s best chance of the match but they’ve failed to convert it. Arsenal’s clean sheet remains intact.

Arteta makes his fifth and final substitution as Calafiori, who recorded the assist for Arsenal’s opener, is withdrawn for Hincapie.

Lampard responds with his own alteration, bringing Hamer on for Tchaouna.

Coventry are still waiting for their first shot on target this evening. Arsenal are seeing this game out with exemplary professionalism.

Odegaard and Tzolis are the next players to leave the field. Eze and World Cup winner Merino are on as their replacements. Arteta’s substitutions tonight have underlined Arsenal’s tremendous squad depth, and that is without the involvement of both Guimaraes and Konsa.

Lewis-Skelly tries to slide a pinpoint pass through to Calafiori, in an attempt to recreate Arsenal’s opening goal from their Community Shield triumph. It nutmegs Torp, but Rushworth makes a quick dash off his line to collect the ball and eliminate any danger.

Lampard adds some fresh legs and orders a double change. Awoniyi, who makes his Coventry debut, and Rudoni are on, with Simms and Thomas-Asante taken off.

Here come some Arsenal changes. Rice and Saka depart to loud ovations, with Zubimendi and Madueke on to replace them.

Tzolis motors into the Coventry penalty area once again and picks out Havertz, who makes a intelligent run across the six-yard box. Before he can cross or shoot, Thomas sprints over to make an interception.

The visitors then fail to clear a corner and Tzolis slams a low, powerful effort at goal. Rushworth gets down low and spills it, but Thomas is there to hack it away.

Lampard makes the first change of the match for either side as Torp replaces Yirenkyi, whose endured a difficult debut in central midfield for his new side.

Odegaard is enjoying himself out there this evening. Just as he did against Manchester City, he’s playing with such authority, purpose and confidence.

The ball breaks to Tzolis who unleashes a venomous effort at goal. It takes a big deflection and flies out for a corner.

From a Coventry corner, Arsenal counter attack with such intensity and speed. The move ends as Odegaard attempts to find Tzolis with a through ball, but the Norwegian overhits the pass and delayed it too long. The offside flag is then raised against Tzolis.

Van Ewijk attempts to find Simms with a chipped cross towards the back post, but it’s marginally over the striker’s head as Coventry step up their search to pull a goal back.

It’s a nightmare start to the second half for Coventry. Whatever Arteta said to his players at the break has worked wonders.

Lewis-Skelly then shoots from long range and his shot is tipped over the bar by Rushworth.

White overlaps Saka and latches onto the winger’s pass. Saka then tees up Odegaard, who scuffs his close-range effort. Rushworth is wrong-footed and despite getting a glove to it, the ball trickles into the net and Arsenal are cruising.

It's Martin Odegaard... Arsenal have three! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/LrqSSGJWE6

Odegaard has scored some beautiful goals in an Arsenal shirt. That wasn’t one of them. He won’t care, though. Two goals in two games for the Arsenal captain.

Read more about his return to form here: https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2026/08/21/odegaard-a-man-possessed-in-bid-to-unlock-arsenal-attack/

We are back under way for the second half. Will Arsenal add more goals to their tally or can Coventry produce a memorable comeback?

It’s been a steep learning curve for the newly-promoted side, who have been overpowered and outclassed by Arsenal’s quality.

Arsenal are in complete control thanks to a commanding first half display against Coventry. Havertz and Saka have the goals, with the reigning Premier League champions on course to claim a routine three points to kickstart their title defence.

Once again, Saka plays a short corner. Odegaard then passes to Rice, who is in acres of space on the edge of the penalty area. The midfielder shoots, but his curling effort drifts narrowly wide of the far post.

There will be two minutes of added time at the end of this half.

The ball bobbles into Tchaouna’s path and the winger tries a very ambitious acrobatic effort from the edge of the box. It had Raya worried for a second, but the effort lands on the roof of the net. That would have been a spectacular goal if it had sneaked in.

Tzolis teases Thomas and works some space before clipping a cross in towards Havertz. The forward doesn’t connect with the header and Coventry scramble it clear.

Odegaard is pulling the strings and slips a delightful pass through to the onrushing White, who finds himself very far forward, but the right back is swiftly closed down by Coventry’s defence as he shoots.

At the other end, Simms does brilliantly to turn Gabriel and win a free kick just outside the box. The Brazilian centre back picks up a yellow card for his troubles.

Coventry are feeling the full effects of the stark difference in levels between Championship and Premier League. Arsenal look streets ahead at the moment.

Christos Tzolis has only played a few games for Arsenal but it’s already easy to see why he registered 29 assists for Club Brugge last season. He has shown on numerous occasions this summer that he is willing to cross the ball as soon as he receives it. No delay, no faff. It worked against Manchester City last weekend and it created Saka’s goal here.

Welcome back to the Premier League, Coventry... It’s been a chastening opening 27 minutes for Lampard’s side.

Yirenkyi then receives a yellow card on his debut for pulling Lewis-Skelly’s shirt.

Rice strides through midfield and plays a one-two with Odegaard. The English midfielder tees up Tzolis, whose fires a cross into the corridor of uncertainty. Rushworth parries it into the danger zone, gifting an unmarked Saka a simple finish from close range. What a start for the champions!

"Saka couldn't miss!"Arsenal are cruising against Coventry as Bukayo Saka fires home from close range 💥 pic.twitter.com/er411Bi1wh

Arsenal are purring and oozing confidence. Coventry need to be careful and must stay in this game. They cannot allow Arsenal to get a second and run away with this.

Coventry had started well but their first error in defence was ruthlessly punished. That’s Havertz’s 10th goal in his last 17 matches for club and country (including pre-season friendlies). After such an injury-disrupted campaign last year, he’s had a very good summer.

Van Ewijk fails to clear his lines and he’s closed down by Tzolis. The ball ricochets into Calafiori’s path and the left back picks out Havertz with a low cross.

The German sweeps a composed shot into the bottom corner. It’s such a cultured finish and Arsenal begin their defence of the Premier League with a 1-0 lead after 15 minutes.

"The champions are on their way!" Kai Havertz sweeps home from the edge of the box to give Arsenal an early lead against Coventry 👏 pic.twitter.com/SNtrMSPkYJ

Some steady possession for Coventry, who are looking to take the sting and excitement out of the game while also calming the buoyant Arsenal fans down.

Tzolis pops up on the right wing and latches onto Rice’s pass. The attacker then delivers a first-time cross into the box which finds Saka, whose half-volley is blocked by Amenda.

Arsenal then work a short corner that ends with White teeing up Tzolis, but his low strike is smothered by Coventry’s defence. Tzolis has certainly made a lively start, and unsurprisingly, Arsenal’s set pieces are causing some early problems.

Tzolis looks dangerous as he dribbles at Van Ewijk, before cutting inside and unleashing a powerful shot. However, his effort is high and wide. Nevertheless, it’s positive play from Arsenal’s new signing.

Following that Coventry corner, the Premier League holders have monopolised the possession in the early minutes. Chants of ‘Champions of England, we know what we are’ ring around the stadium thanks to the home support, who are in full voice.

Coventry get us under way and the newly-promoted side have won an early corner, which is comfortably dealt with by Arsenal’s defence.

The atmosphere at the Emirates is electric. Can Arsenal flex their title-winning credentials once again or will Coventry cause an almighty upset?

New Arsenal signing Ezri Konsa has been presented on the pitch, with both sets of players set to follow him any moment now.

The 2026-27 season is just minutes away from kicking off.

Coventry have recruited some powerful, aggressive players this summer. They will be looking to frustrate Arsenal by shutting down the spaces around their penalty area, and they will certainly be competitive at set-pieces.

Meanwhile, the Arsenal fans have just had their first glimpse of Ezri Konsa in the club’s shirt. The new signing walked out onto the pitch to wave to the supporters.

With just over five minutes until the 2026-27 Premier League season starts, here are tonight’s teams in full...

Arsenal: Raya, White, Mosquera, Gabriel, Calafiori, Odegaard, Rice, Lewis-Skelly, Saka, Havertz, Tzolis.

Subs: Arrizabalaga, Hincapie, Eze, Gyokeres, Madueke, Nwaneri, Merino, Zubimendi, Dowman.

Coventry: Rushworth, van Ewijk, Thomas, Amenda, Dasilva, Onyeka, Yirenkyi, Grimes, Thomas-Asante, Simms, Tchaouna.

Subs: Wilson, Rudoni, Sakamoto, Awoniyi, Kitching, Latibeaudiere, Eccles, Overgaard, Hamer.

Speaking to Sky Sports, the Arsenal boss said: “He had a slight tension in his groin. He hasn’t done a pre-season, he only had four or five days before that [Man City] game. We have to take a lot of new stuff for him as well. We need to take it bit by bit.”

Another game, another snub for Gabriel Martinelli. As was the case against Manchester City in last weekend’s Community Shield, the Brazilian isn’t even on the bench tonight. It’s quite clear what’s going on here: Arsenal need to make sales and he is an obvious candidate to depart. It’s not particularly pleasant, though, and you can’t help but feel for a player who has been so important to this club over the last seven years.

Martinelli has made it clear he does not want to move to Galatasary, who made an offer recently. Will a more suitable club come forward for him? We’ll find out in the coming days.

In two full seasons at Coventry between 2021 and 2023, Viktor Gyokeres scored 40 goals in 97 games for Coventry, and was part of the side that lost on penalties to Luton Town in the Championship play-off final to Luton Town.

If Coventry had won that game, would Gyokeres still be wearing a sky blue shirt instead of joining Sporting CP and then Arsenal, who knows...

The striker will have to wait to get onto the pitch against his former team, with Mikel Arteta choosing Kai Havertz to lead the line.

Odegaard comes into the new Premier League season, which begins when Arsenal host Coventry City on Friday night, with a point to prove. That may sound unusual, given his new-found status as a title-winning captain, but last year was a strange one for the 27-year-old. The club’s most successful campaign of his time at Arsenal was also the most frustrating one for Odegaard as an individual.

Last season, Arsenal clinched a much-anticipated Premier League title for the first time in 22 years and are the favourites to lift the trophy for a second successive season. Mikel Arteta’s side have recently claimed the Community Shield and look like they mean business.

Arsenal are clearly not resting on their laurels in their bid to win another top-flight title, having strengthened their squad this summer with the signings of Bruno Guimarães, Christos Tzolis and Ezri Konsa.

Arteta looks raring to go and ready to mount another title charge.

"Everything has to start with me" 💪Mikel Arteta says Arsenal are ready for the new Premier League season 💥 pic.twitter.com/rsUcs7ot7T

After last season’s Championship by a whopping 95 points under Frank Lampard’s management, Coventry head into their first Premier League campaign since suffering relegation from the competition in 2001.

Coventry were playing in the fourth tier as recently as 2017, so lining up against the Premier League holders is a full-circle moment for the club and supporters that is richly deserved.

"I loved it, I loved driving here, feeling the atmosphere, the fans" Frank Lampard on what tonight means for him and Coventry 😍Watch live here: https://t.co/0AejI4B8dF pic.twitter.com/077Bga2Z4W

On Friday night, at the home of champions Arsenal, Coventry officially begin a new chapter back in the Premier League and expectations will be high. The man responsible for that tidal wave of optimism is Lampard, their promotion hero.

He has proved a transformative appointment since arriving in November 2024, and the former England and Chelsea captain is relishing the chance to rattle some cages.

His return is a feel-good story and Lampard has a point to prove. He admits that the desire to upset his detractors drives him on. “I’ve got experience of the Premier League and hopefully I can get that across to the players,” he said.

“The club has been out of this division for 25 years so of course it’s exciting. We want to challenge and we want to do well. I’m pleased that we’re here and you want to work at the top. We’re very focused on the job.”

Arsenal ruined Enzo Maresca’s first competitive outing as Man City’s new manager in the club’s first match without Pep Guardiola. It was one-way traffic as Arsenal cruised to a resounding 3-0 win to lift the Community Shield in Cardiff.

Riccardo Calafiori opened the scoring just 23 seconds after he was brilliantly played in by Myles Lewis-Skelly’s defence-splitting pass. Arsenal doubled their lead before the half-hour mark through Kai Havertz’s close-range header and Martin Odegaard added a sumptuously taken third shortly after the interval.

The Premier League holders were in a ruthless mood and completely overran their opponents. Christos Tzolis grabbed two assists out on the left wing, Bruno Guimarães produced a typically commanding performance in the first half and Odegaard controlled proceedings with his creativity.

It was an early taste of silverware for Mikel Arteta’s men, who are the overwhelming favourites to retain their Premier League crown.

"I'm really pleased, that's a really good team" Ian Wright is happy with the Arsenal starting XI to face Coventry, do you agree? 💬 Watch live: https://t.co/0AejI4B8dF pic.twitter.com/IUBlMS963w

New signings Aurele Amenda, Loum Tchaouna and Caleb Yirenkyi all start and make their Coventry debuts this evening.

Carl Rushworth and Frank Onyeka also begin from the outset after making their moves permanent following successful loans last season.

Your City tonight. 📋 pic.twitter.com/V0nzaemLYF

As Sam Dean confirmed earlier on, Bruno Guimaraes is absent from the squad. The Brazilian was subbed off at half-time in the dominant Community Shield victory over Manchester City with a thigh issue.

Both Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka start after being used off the bench in the Community Shield last weekend, with Guimaraes and Noni Madueke dropping to the bench.

To soften the blow of Bruno Guimaraes’ absence from tonight’s squad due to injury, the Premier League holders can rejoice over the signing of Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa for over £50m.

The centre back has penned a four-year deal with the option of a further year.

Speaking to Arsenal’s official website, Sporting Director Andrea Berta said: “Ezri is a defender of high quality, whose athleticism, composure and tactical intelligence have established him as one of the Premier League’s most consistent performers.

“Being comfortable in both central defence and at right-back, Ezri will bring valuable versatility to our squad while maintaining the high defensive standards which are fundamental to our challenge of winning major trophies.”

Konsa will play no role in tonight’s encounter, having only completed the move earlier in the day.

Reinforcing the backline ✍️ pic.twitter.com/deYQhZcmOy

Good evening and welcome to the Emirates Stadium, where the Premier League champions begin the defence of their title. Or, as Mikel Arteta prefers to put it, their “attack” on a new season. A classic Arteta-ism.

The assault starts tonight against Coventry City but our understanding is that Arsenal will be without new £75m midfielder Bruno Guimaraes. We believe the Brazilian has picked up an injury, and it’s not currently clear how severe it might be. Clearly, this is a blow for Arteta. But they should still have enough to get past promoted Coventry… shouldn’t they? We’ll find out soon enough.

Meanwhile, Arteta has said he and his players should relish being Premier League title favourites and the role of the hunted rather than the hunter.

“In the last three seasons, at some point we were first and at some point we were chasing. And you never know what is better,” Arteta said. “But if you give me the choice, I want to be first. I want to be hunted, and I want to be in control of our future, rather than depending on somebody else.”

Arteta called on his players to retain the hunger they had last season.

“We start from scratch, from zero, and we’re going to have to prove we are at the level to go back to that position again,” he said. “We need to show that desire and the ambition to be better than what we were last season, a month ago, a week ago.”

This is Coventry’s first Premier League campaign since they suffered relegation in 2000-01, and they were led to the Championship title by Frank Lampard. They scored the most goals in the Championship and conceded the fewest, and could face one of their former players tonight in Viktor Gyokeres.

#1688. Opinion: Liverpool now have to utilise 83-goal star after Arsenal defeat

Liverpool lost their second game of the season on the Sunday.

The Reds were facing Arsenal in a game which could have propelled them into the Premier League title race.

Instead, one mistake led to Mikel Arteta's men sitting back for most of the clash after they'd bagged their first goal.

Obviously, shutting up shop works for the Gunners but, it still feels like Liverpool should have done much better than they did.

They had barely any shots on target despite their attack being their most expensive ever.

Fans have been questioning whether Andoni Iraola is the right fit for Liverpool and now, questions are even being asked about some of his players with fans wanting the Spaniard to utilise every single option he has at his disposal.

Andoni Iraola confirms Liverpool should have done better with the chances that they had

Liverpool may have had four shots on target throughout their game against Arsenal on Sunday but, they didn't manage to convert any of them into goals.

Bradley Barcola and Alexander Isak both kept coming up short which, for a duo who cost almost £250 million between them, is far from ideal.

This is why fans can't wait for Hugo Ekitike to return as, before he got injured last term, he was easily the Reds' best attacker and managed to convert almost every chance he was given.

But, now that he's not been available for a while, the cracks among Liverpool's attack are really starting to show.

In fact, after their defeat against Arsenal on Sunday, Iraola even said himself that his men should have done a lot better with the chances that they had.

"We had big chances. Cross bar, real big chances. We should have scored, and had enough to score today," he said in quotes relayed by Anfield Sector.

Federico Chiesa could help Liverpool convert their chances more often

Among their ranks, Liverpool have a fair few forgotten players.

However, none are as forgotten as Federico Chiesa. The Italian was brought in by Liverpool during Arne Slot's first season in charge with fans thinking that his £10 million fee was the bargain of the century.

But, after he returned from his ACL tear at Juventus, he was just never the same player which is why the Italian giants were probably so keen to get rid of him.

Now that he's back fit, fans thought Iraola would at least give him a chance to prove his worth but, he's not been given that privilege yet.

However, even though this hasn't happened yet, it doesn't mean that he still doesn't have stuff to offer Liverpool.

Throughout his career, he's bagged 83 goals and, the fact that he can play anywhere across the front three is another massive selling point.

Right now, Iraola is clearly trying to find his best front three so, even just giving Chiesa the chance to prove his worth could help him get closer to that.

Here's hoping that, before the January transfer window comes around, the Italian is given a chance.

Barcelona have been through a run of tricky games, losing their 100% record in the Champions League and La Liga to Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid, and now, after recovering with two wins, they face another big challenge. On Tuesday, Barcelona host Aston Villa at the Camp Nou.

The English side have won every game in the European competition and are unbeaten in five Premier League matches. That is why Pau Torres, an undisputed starter for Aston Villa, is not afraid at all of the game against Barcelona.

Barcelona, under the management of Hansi Flick, are characterised by heavy pressing in the attacking half, which forces a high defensive line to keep up with the rest of the team. That space is something for Aston Villa to exploit, as Pau Torres explained, based on the profile of their trio of very quick attackers, including a Brazilian.

‘This year we have very vertical players, such as Ibrahim Mbaye, Alysson and Nicolas Jackson himself. They work very well when opponents leave space behind the defence.’

Of course, there is a way to attack, but for more than 60% of the time Barcelona’s opponents will be defending. Focus is a must if they are to avoid conceding against Barcelona, who have scored 57 times in 14 matches this season. ‘If we want to get a positive result, we will have to be alert defensively.’

Pau Torres also has a special mission. As a left-sided centre-back, he could come up against right winger Lamine Yamal several times because of the cover he will have to provide for left-back Ian Maatsen, who is known for being very attacking.

‘When you play this type of match, you always want to face the best to find out what level you are at. It will be a pleasure to play against Lamine and have to mark him on some occasions.

#1686. Guys like Makhanya and Sterling should feel welcome to speak the truth more often if Rangers are to finally throw off their serial losers tag

Published: 14:15 EDT, 30 October 2026 | Updated: 15:19 EDT, 30 October 2026

Olwethu Makhanya is shaping up to be everything Rangers needed in their search for defensive reinforcements in the summer.

A solid presence at the back, a young and hungry talent very much on the up and a leader with real personality.

If it didn’t look so likely that someone will come in before long and offer the Ibrox board the chance to make a healthy profit on the £3million they paid to Philadelphia Union for the 22-year-old, you’d put him down as a nailed-on future captain.

He’s helping set the standards required if Rangers are to overhaul arch-rivals Celtic in the title race and was absolutely spot-on after rescuing an ill-deserved point with a late equaliser at Tynecastle on Wednesday when bemoaning a lack of character at the start of the second half and the fact Hearts worked harder and showed more desire.

It’s the kind of honesty many Ibrox sides of recent years have needed. A public kick up the backside for underperforming team-mates, the footballing equivalent of getting the whip out and a necessary form of assurance for frustrated supporters that there is at least someone inside the dressing room who feels the way they feel, who wants what they want.

It’s why it is to be hoped that manager Derek McInnes’ remarks the morning after were not some attempt to gently slap down the South African.

Defender Olwethu Makhanya questioned the character of this Rangers squad midweek

McInnes, of course, is entitled to his own opinion about the reserves of character within his squad. Maybe he did disagree with Makhanya’s version of events, or his questioning of the side’s resilience.

Alternative viewpoints delivered respectfully are fine. More than fine. They are a sign of a healthy workplace.

It just felt like it was all skirting a little too close to a chastisement of the big centre-back’s comments.

And whether that was the intention or not, being seen to chastise a player whose sentiments are clearly coming from the right place, from a burning desire to make a club with one league crown in 15 years be successful again, is not necessarily the right course of action to take.

It happened, if you remember, with Dujon Sterling back in Philippe Clement’s first season as boss when an April collapse that involved a home draw with Celtic, a 3-2 loss at Ross County and a stalemate at Dundee pretty much killed off hopes of lifting the title.

‘We owe ourselves a performance… because we have been s**t the past three games,’ said Sterling in the aftermath at Dens Park. ‘We are fighting for a title and the way we are playing, it is as if we are not playing for anything. It’s like the season is dead and it is a dead-rubber game.’

It felt like a cry from the heart, a desperate plea to those around him to breathe life into a dying campaign. It was a truth that had to be told.

Clement, meanwhile, was already well on the way to losing the plot at that point, claiming his side were ‘moral winners’ after snatching that draw with Celtic thanks to a late goal and insisting that he was happy his side ‘bossed it’ at Dens.

Criticising Sterling afterwards just made him look even more like he didn’t get it, had lost all sight of what being at Rangers — or any club that has to win at all costs — was about.

‘It’s the words of a player who is disappointed because we lost points and maybe lacks a bit of experience in that way,’ stated the Belgian waffler. ‘That’s things for young players to learn and become better in. It’s more talking out of frustration.’

Manager Derek McInnes disagreed with Makhanya's comments following the Hearts game

That’s the standard response from football persons, of course. The whole business, for some time, has revolved around young players having it battered into them that it’s better to say nothing, to drone on dead-eyed through interviews, bat everything away, put their personality on the bonfire, ‘don’t get too up or too down’.

It’s nonsense, though. McInnes honed his trade in a Nine-In-A-Row Rangers dressing room full of huge characters who built unbreakable bonds while still being able to dig each other out, demand more, be confrontational.

Sure, it happened more behind doors than in the public gaze, but things are different now from the way they were 30 years ago. Social media has changed the landscape so drastically. Fan narratives do drive boardroom decisions and that has arguably been clearer at Ibrox in recent times than anywhere.

There’s a concern still living just under the surface among a large number of Rangers fans that there is an ingrained loser mentality at their club and plenty of evidence to back that up.

Admittedly, the playing staff has changed drastically since then, but it is impossible to forget Billy Dodds reflecting on his time as a first-team coach for interim boss Barry Ferguson and talking about how 70 per cent of signings had been wrong and that the dressing room had a number of weak characters who couldn’t handle adversity.

Even before Danny Rohl left for Red Bull Salzburg last season, he talked about players being ‘too lazy to recover’ in key moments. He also spoke about how some of the squad were ‘very quiet’ when he first took over.

Supporters of Rangers, treated to some amount of failure and in-house claptrap over the last decade or more, need to see evidence that those on the field care the way they do.

The kind of frank analysis delivered by Makhanya — in a calm and considered way, it should be said — need not be the negative so many inside football are programmed to think.

If anything, seeing guys wear their hearts on their sleeve can serve to strengthen the relationship between fans and their favourites in difficult times.

The modern-day audience have had enough of failing players promising to learn lessons and move on. At outfits judged on league titles and facing pressure to win every week, learning lessons is the last thing on the agenda. You really ought to know what needs done by that stage.

Rangers have drawn two of their last three and currently trail leaders Celtic by four points

Punters want to see the real people behind the branding, measure their minerals. And we’re on about more than just those cringeworthy features on club TV where players quiz each other on whether they prefer Jaffa Cakes or KitKats while playing a game of ping-pong. It’s showing a bit of what’s really inside, being properly authentic, that resonates.

In fairness to McInnes, his messaging as Rangers boss has generally been good so far. He didn’t shy away from the paucity of those performances in losing in Europe to Jagiellonia Bialystok and Jablonec.

He hasn’t indulged in deflection. He confronted the speculation that was already beginning to swirl about his future after that Jablonec catastrophe, handled it well and steered the side to safer ground with two excellent back-to-back wins against Celtic.

He has been honest and upfront and entirely understanding of the expectations that rest upon his shoulders.

His team is still guilty of switching off in games. Centre-back Manny Fernandez, although the manager must back him publicly, is the epitome of that.

His players still have to show they can be consistent enough to prevail against a Celtic side that is most definitely there for the taking. They need to keep the pedal to the metal and to deliver 90-minute performances or, at least, maintain control throughout.

It is a squad light on trophies on the CV and with a number of younger players. It is going to need regular reminders as this race plays out.

If Makhanya or Sterling or anyone else want to take it upon themselves to put those reminders out there, it shouldn’t be regarded as a bad thing. And it definitely shouldn’t be discouraged.

#1684. GdS: How Amorim’s fluidity helped Rabiot record career-best start to a season

Adrien Rabiot continues to deliver in the biggest games for AC Milan, and Ruben Amorim is arguably getting the best ever form out of him.

La Gazzetta dello Sport begin a report by recalling how different things were in the summer. With Milan falling to fifth and Massmiliano Allegri being sacked, many presumed that Rabiot could follow him to Napoli, to play Champions League football.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Rabiot not only remained at Milanello, but is also the Atlas of the team this year. He carries it on his shoulders and takes its weight with disarming ease and personality. While Allegri observes Milan from below, Adrien has found a new coach who is giving him a new lease of life.

The derby goal is an excellent indicator of Rabiot’s confidence, attempting that billiard-like shot (even though some, like Yunus Musah, maintain it was a cross) in a match like this, with the game still wide open, signifies complete self-confidence.

The Frenchman knows perfectly well he has a powerful shot, but he opted for finesse, guiding the ball to kiss the post and land in the back of the net as eleven Nerazzurri players watched it slowly and mockingly cross their penalty area.

Rabiot was one of the derby’s heroes but has been performing at a high level for several matches now. He currently has the best average rating in the squad, and it’s a stratospheric 6.81 (out of 10, across all games).

The other key number is nine: five goals and four assists this season makes nine contributions, the most in the squad. In the league, he’s been involved in a goal in each of his last five games: assists against Lazio, goals against Lecce and Sassuolo, a goal and assist against Atalanta, and a goal in the derby.

To better understand his further improvement from an already very high level, we must consider that in the entire last season, Adrien had six goals and four assists. He’s one goal away from matching that tally.

Some tactical considerations help contextualise things. Compared to Allegri, Amorim’s style of football is on another level, being much more attacking. It’s not based solely on counter-attacks, but on a flow of play that starts from midfield and allows for the runs of those who move in between the lines.

Rabiot has always been a player who can get forward: he has the physique, technique, and footballing intelligence. Amorim has given him a further step because he’s made him more difficult to read for opponents.

If before, the Frenchman was a classic pivot midfielder, now you find him practically everywhere. At the start of the season, Amorim’s style of football was positional, locked into a 3-4-2-1 that seemed set in stone with Rabiot behind the striker.

Then the Portuguese coach realised he was doing himself harm and began a tactical overhaul. The fundamentalist has become fluid, and the playing system is now an abstract concept that must be filled with individual interpretations.

This is a set of circumstances where Rabiot shines. The derby is a perfect example: the former PSG man was everywhere, depending on his own tendencies and the team’s need for certain characteristics in certain parts if the pitch.

This is the best start to a season of his career. Now, in addition to the pitch, he’ll also have to keep an eye on his desk. After Strahinja Pavlovic and Christian Pulisic, he’s the next one destined to ascend to the fourth floor of Casa Milan to sign a renewal waiting for him.

#1683. Man Utd next manager: Unai Emery to Old Trafford latest as fresh update emerges on Carrick replacement

By Lewis Blain | 03 Nov 2026 07:07

Manchester United continue to admire Aston Villa manager Unai Emery as they consider potential alternatives should Michael Carrick leave Old Trafford.

However, convincing the Spaniard to abandon his successful project at Villa Park could prove extremely difficult, with questions over how much authority he would receive in Manchester.

Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann are also emerging as leading contenders, potentially giving the Red Devils several alternative options in their managerial search.

According to TEAMtalk, United decision-makers still highly regard Emery, and the club continues to explore potential replacements for Carrick behind the scenes.

The Spaniard has transformed Aston Villa into top-four contenders and guided them to Europa League success, establishing significant influence over the club's footballing operations.

That control has been central to his achievements, and Villa would be expected to fight hard to retain their manager if United formalised their interest.

Although the opportunity to take charge of one of Europe's biggest clubs could appeal to Emery, sources believe the level of authority available at Old Trafford would be a major stumbling block.

At Villa, Emery has been allowed considerable freedom over his methods and decision-making. United's structure and expectations are different, potentially making the role less attractive than it initially appears.

United are understood to be preparing for different scenarios despite publicly backing Carrick, with Emery remaining among the names held in high regard internally.

Former Newcastle United boss Howe is also heavily linked, with director of football Jason Wilcox reportedly favouring him. Meanwhile, director of recruitment Christopher Vivell is believed to prefer Nagelsmann.

Emery would be an impressive appointment on paper, but United may be wasting valuable time pursuing a manager who has little obvious reason to leave Villa.

He has built a successful project at Villa Park, enjoys considerable control and has established the club as a regular competitor for major honours.

Moving to Old Trafford would mean taking on a rebuilding job at a club that has struggled with managerial instability for more than a decade. There is no guarantee he would receive the same influence that has helped him thrive in Birmingham.

United should therefore concentrate on more realistic alternatives, with Howe potentially offering an attractive option given his Premier League experience and previous success at Newcastle.

Nagelsmann also deserves serious consideration, particularly if Vivell can convince the club's hierarchy that he is the right long-term appointment.

Emery's reputation makes him an understandable target, but United need a manager who genuinely wants the job and can work within their structure. On the available evidence, Howe and Nagelsmann may be more realistic options.

Arsenal star Max Dowman (second from right) looks shocked after the referee shows him a red card at Fleetwood Town

Manager Mikel Arteta has words with the distraught youngster as he leaves the field

Arteta said: ‘I haven't seen the reaction to my reaction. But you have to understand the context, the relationship that I have with him and what we discussed just before we went out.

‘You want to always have the best reaction, the beautiful one. But do you want to see the reaction of his team-mates when they have to play with the 10 men, you want to see that? What do you expect?

‘I don't know. Or the England (Under 16) ones, they are his age, 16, the same. What is their reaction?

‘Whether it’s right or wrong, that's the reaction. And the reaction when I don't win, you know what is? I’m p***** off big time.

‘We have to be ready for that, this is the environment and this is the reality. Otherwise we are in Disneyland. We are not in Disneyland, we are in the Premier League at this level.

‘We look after him so much that you cannot imagine, and at the same time we are going to be demanding that anybody continues to earn the right to play. Otherwise what are the rest of the boys going to tell me? It needs to be fair, that's all.’

He further explained that his touchline reaction was borne out of frustration having told Dowman to not react to such a scenario before the game.

‘I thought we discussed that before the game,’ the Spaniard said. ‘It was related to what could happen. Not only the red, but the 10 seconds before, the way he (Dowman) comes to receive the ball, what kind of ball that is, and after that if he gets tackled, what happens next. Exactly that.’

Arteta revealed he had spoken with Dowman about the incident. 'I had a talk with him yesterday,' he said. 'No issue at all. I've done it, so I try to prevent that.

'That's why I'm so protective of these things, and especially with young players, because we have made those mistakes. And you know how much you can get punished and how much it can change what happens next.'

On the FA’s decision to reject the Gunners’ red card appeal, he said: ‘Very disappointed, to be fair. Especially with the reckless tackles that he received, and then his reaction is minimal in relation to the action.

‘(We’re) disappointed that it's not been overturned after looking at the action back.

‘We have put every argument on the table to make a case for it. Not only the action, but when you look back at it in slow motion, the previous action and Max's action, it's clear that obviously we have a very different opinion.

‘And on top of that, I think you have to read the context of the player, the age.’

The severity of the challenge is also an issue for Arteta. ‘It could have been really bad, yeah,’ he said. ‘And we are lucky today that he hasn't had a broken foot. That's clear.’

#1680. Real Madrid: how Franco Mastantuono is faring on loan at Fiorentina

By Axel Clody | 03 Nov 2026 07:08

Franco Mastantuono has finally been getting consecutive opportunities in European football. After a first year of ups and downs at Real Madrid, the young Argentine was loaned to Fiorentina this season and has played in all of the club’s games.

The high point of his spell, which began in August, has been the hat-trick against Venezia in the fourth round of Serie A, a 4-2 comeback win that made him the youngest Argentine player to score three times in Europe’s top five leagues. The first two goals were very much in the right winger’s style: cutting inside onto his left foot and placing the finish.

That result, however, was the only time the Florence side managed to win in Serie A. Fiorentina’s campaign has produced six defeats and two draws, which is why they sit on the edge of the relegation zone.

Mastantuono has not been involved in a goal since, even though he remains the team’s main attacking protagonist. One of the reasons lies in the young player’s biggest challenge so far in Italy, which he admitted himself in an interview shortly after arriving in the country.

Responsible for a third of his team’s league goals, the 19-year-old forward carries the responsibility of being the ‘owner’ of the attacking department in the side managed by Paolo Vanoli. He is always sought out on the wing for an individual move and delivers: he is the leader in ground duels won in the whole of Serie A (48, along with two other players) and third in successful dribbles, 18, alongside Nico Paz.

‘I am always looking to attack, going at opponents and showing personality’ - he explained his profile to the newspaper Gazzetta dello Sport on 4 September.

Thanks to his ability to win individual duels, he also constantly puts himself in a position to shoot, and is third in that statistic in the league too (33, the leader in the Fiorentina squad). He also provides passes for his team-mates’ shots (17 in all, 17th in the league and top in the squad).

The Argentine generates a lot of attacking play, that is undeniable, but the finishing of moves has almost always been negative. He has attempted 33 shots but only nine have been on target. ‘I need to improve in many things, including my efficiency in front of goal,’ he admitted, also to Gazzetta.

Another feature of his game, dribbling, also has issues that hamper Fiorentina and kill the team’s attacks. Mastantuono often wins a one-on-one and, instead of passing the ball, tries another, which makes him lose it.

His success rate in dribbles and ground duels is below half of those attempted (43% and 48% respectively). Among all Serie A players, he is second for possession losses, with 20. Manager Vanoli has already identified the issue, praising the youngster as the only one capable of setting the team’s tempo.

‘He is a talent who needs to be put at the service of the team and must improve his understanding of when to dictate the team’s rhythm. He is the only one who can do that. I told him that, in Italy, we are good at noticing when a player wants to dribble. He needs to improve in one-on-one situations and understand that, if he is double-marked, there will always be a team-mate free. And that means playing as a team’ - he said on 23 October.

This, however, is still common for Franco Mastantuono’s age. It is a natural maturing process. He still looks a very promising youngster, to the same extent as when he emerged at River Plate. He does not see much fairness in the criticism he receives.

‘People demand a lot of me. I understand, I know what they expect of me. Many times they are hard on me, but I try to make the most of it. [...] I do not complain about criticism.

I am a footballer and I understand that. But people talk about things that are outside my control. I just do my job and always try to do it well’ - he told TyC Sports in early October.

Mastantuono is answering some of that criticism on the pitch and, after the frustration of missing the World Cup because of his few minutes at Real Madrid, he was part of Argentina’s latest call-up. The forward, like Nico Paz and other youngsters, will be the future of Argentina in a new era without Lionel Messi and other experienced players.

#1678. Report: Liverpool star now wanted by Real Madrid, it's not Alexis Mac Allister

Andoni Iraola still has a lot of work to do on his Liverpool squad.

Even though the Spaniard has only lost two games as the Reds' manager, it still feels like a lot more could come from him.

Last term, he managed to exceed expectations with Bournemouth and, most fans thought that he'd bring his heavy metal style of football to L4.

However, that evidently hasn't been the case with Liverpool failing to register a single shot on target against Arsenal on Sunday.

This poor form hasn't stopped clubs from showing an interest in the Reds' players with Real Madrid now monitoring a member of Liverpool's first-team squad.

Real Madrid are monitoring Victor Munoz ahead of a possible return

This summer, Liverpool spent over £150 million on new players.

Four new faces were added to the Reds' ranks and, even though Jeremy Jacquet's transfer was already confirmed back in January, he's still a new player for Liverpool to use.

And, even though he's been in fine form, it's not him who Real Madrid want, it's Victor Munoz.

"The club is keeping a close eye on all of them, and it is no secret that the two Como players are forcing their way into the conversation through their performances," Diario Sport wrote.

"Still, no firm decision has been made. Those in charge do not believe this is the right stage of the season to make such calls. A player’s form and confidence can change dramatically between now and the moment a return is actually considered.

"That was the case with Paz last season, when an apparently certain return to Madrid ultimately gave way to the player’s determination to remain at Como. Rafa Marín and Víctor Muñoz are among the other names still being monitored as possible returnees."

Liverpool cannot afford to let Victor Munoz leave

Over the last few years, Liverpool and Real Madrid have been fairly intertwined with one another.

Whether it's been Los Blancos prising Liverpool's players away for free or meeting them in the Champions League, their paths seem to have crossed on many occasions.

In fact, even with Munoz's transfer to Liverpool this summer, Real Madrid bagged a decent chunk of change from their sell-on clause which probably helped them pay Ibrahima Konate's signing fee.

And, even though the Spaniard may not have been Liverpool's best attacker this season, he's still played a very important role.

The £35 million that the Reds paid for Munoz was a steal and, right now, he's one of their best options on the right wing.

Here's hoping that Real Madrid don't put in an offer and end up turning their attention towards someone else.

#1676. O'Neill hits out at critics as Celtic boss issues surprising response to McGregor's midweek comments

By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER

Published: 15:03 EDT, 30 October 2026 | Updated: 15:30 EDT, 30 October 2026

Celtic manager Martin O’Neill has claimed some of the club’s critics are only seeking to cause division within the camp.

On the back of a 2-2 draw with Dundee United earlier this week, Celtic skipper Callum McGregor claimed they are playing like a basketball team who lack control in matches.

McGregor also appeared to question the fact that Celtic started the match effectively with three strikers across the frontline in Kasper Hogh, Camilo Duran and Callum Osmand.

‘It’s not really having a nailed-on profile for each of the positions,’ said McGregor. ‘The players behave like a winger, or they behave like a striker.

‘You can get away with it for a few games but if it’s a striker playing as a winger, you are going to get that behaviour a lot of the time.

‘You’ve got enough quality so you can score goals and get away with it. But we have to try to get the team functioning the way it should.

O'Neill is satisfied with Celtic's start to the season despite criticism over performances

‘Then that will alleviate all the other problems that we are encountering, where it becomes a bit like basketball, you lose control and spend the next 15 minutes trying to get possession back.’

At half-time in the game against United at Parkhead, O’Neill took Hogh off and reverted to a more traditional system with Jota and Haissem Hassan coming on as wingers to replace the misfiring Dane and Osmand.

Celtic eventually fought back to claim a point, but McGregor’s comments became the subject of much scrutiny.

It is not the first time a senior player has spoken out this season, with Cameron Carter-Vickers claiming that Celtic’s style of play was ‘random’ after the Old Firm defeats to Rangers.

O’Neill insists he actually agrees with McGregor’s comments — but has vowed to find a solution at the top end of the pitch.

The veteran boss also appeared to snipe back at some of the critics who have claimed that there is unrest among the squad.

‘I’ve said this to you before, I totally agree that Osmand is actually really a centre-forward,’ said O’Neill when asked about McGregor’s verdict.

‘I’ve said it at the press conference, that he is essentially a centre-forward who probably would play off somebody strong alongside him.

‘I'm not so sure that he could lead the line on his own. And that Duran is really a centre-forward.

‘So the players are getting to know each other. It’s really as simple as that. So I’m in total agreement with Callum. We’ll sort it out.

The manager admits that the likes of Camilo Duran are currently being played out of position

‘We seem to be doing okay domestically, trying to sort it out.

‘There’s a few players that haven’t had a chance. [Jordan] Lotomba hasn’t had a chance yet to play. There’ll be moments, absolutely.

‘Young [Joel] Van Den Berg has trained today. So over the course of the next number of weeks, between now and Christmas, I think everybody will be on the field of play.

‘And then it’s a matter of establishing right positions as much as possible.

‘Players have played out of position before. I don’t know whether it was a big issue when young Osmand came on in the Benfica game and set us alight.

‘I come in here [to the press conference] every single week and I’m most of the time pretty buoyed by things.

‘Don’t try and throw a lot of divides in. At the end of the day, we’re doing fine.

‘A lot of lads here didn’t even do pre-season with us. A number of players came in quite late on, so it will take time for us.

‘So we need to hang in there, and at this minute I think we’re hanging in.’

With Rangers playing Aberdeen in the semi-finals of the Premier Sports Cup, Celtic travel to Falkirk tomorrow knowing that a victory would send them seven points clear of their Old Firm rivals.

O'Neill added: ‘I think we’ve done fine, we’re leading the league with a four-point gap at this minute, which is nothing at all at this stage of the season.

‘We fought back and retrieved those kind of leads on a couple of occasions last season.

‘We’ll try and get a result or two in European football which would be nice, but domestically we’ve been fine.

‘Falkirk had a bit of a stodgy start, but they are flying now, so we know it’ll be a difficult game for us.’
